**Rajeev Chandrasekhar** (born 31 May 1964) is an Indian politician, entrepreneur, and technocrat. He currently represents [Nemom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemom_Assembly_constituency "Nemom Assembly constituency") in the 16th [Kerala Legislative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Legislative_Assembly "Kerala Legislative Assembly") since [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Kerala_Legislative_Assembly_election "2026 Kerala Legislative Assembly election"). He is also the state president of [BJP Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BJP_Kerala "BJP Kerala").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajeev_Chandrasekhar#cite_note-1) A prominent voice in India's digital and economic policy, he is a former Union Minister, having served as the Minister of State for the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, and the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

Before his ministerial appointments, Rajeev served as a Member of Parliament (MP) in the Rajya Sabha representing Karnataka for multiple terms between 2006 and 2024. Initially serving as an independent MP elected with broad legislative support, he officially joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in 2018. Within the [National Democratic Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Alliance "National Democratic Alliance") (NDA), he has also held the roles of national spokesperson and vice-chairman of the coalition's Keralam unit.

Throughout his parliamentary career, Rajeev has been instrumental in shaping national policy, serving as a Member of the Joint Committee on the Data Protection Bill, 2019, the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), and the Consultative Committee on MoE & IT. He has also been a member of the Indian Council for World Affairs and served on the Rajya Sabha Select Committees for both the GST and Real Estate bills.

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rajeev_Chandrasekhar&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Rajeev Chandrasekhar was born to a [Malayali Nair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nair "Nair") family[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajeev_Chandrasekhar#cite_note-:0-2) in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. His father, M. K. Chandrasekhar, was an Air Commodore in the Indian Air Force and a trainer of [Rajesh Pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Pilot "Rajesh Pilot"), and his mother is Anandavalli Amma. His family hails from [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajeev_Chandrasekhar#cite_note-:0-2)

Rajeev Chandrasekhar studied at St. Paul's Convent School in Thrissur and completed his schooling at Kendriya Vidyalaya in Bengaluru. He then studied electrical engineering at the Manipal Institute of Technology. He obtained his master's degree in computer science in 1988 from the Illinois Institute of Technology in Chicago.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajeev_Chandrasekhar#cite_note-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rajeev_Chandrasekhar&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Entrepreneur

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rajeev_Chandrasekhar&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Entrepreneur")]

In 1991, after returning to India, Rajeev Chandrasekhar joined the BPL Group. In 1994, he founded BPL Mobile, which grew into one of the major telecom companies in India, holding key licenses in markets such as Mumbai. In July 2005, he sold his 64 per cent stake in BPL Communications to the Essar Group for US$1.1 billion.

Rajeev founded Jupiter Capital in 2005, with an initial investment of US$100 million. The investment firm has investments and managed assets of over US$800 million in technology, media, hospitality, and entertainment.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajeev_Chandrasekhar#cite_note-auto-4)

In April 2013, Rajeev was awarded an honorary degree by Visvesvaraya Technological University, Belgaum, in recognition of his work as an entrepreneur.

### Media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rajeev_Chandrasekhar&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Media")]

In 2006, Rajeev Chandrasekhar expanded into media by acquiring a majority stake in Asianet Communications through Jupiter Capital Private Limited. In late 2008, he formed a joint venture with News Corp, establishing Asianet Star Communications.

Asianet News Network Private Limited, incorporated in May 2008 under his leadership, serves as the holding company for key outlets including Asianet News, Asianet Suvarna News, and the digital portal Newsable.

In 2016, his group invested approximately ₹60 crore in ARG Outlier Media, supporting the launch of Republic TV. Following his election to the Rajya Sabha as a BJP member in 2018, the stake was diluted in compliance with parliamentary disclosure norms in 2019.

### Politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rajeev_Chandrasekhar&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Politics")]

**Member of Parliament**

Rajeev began his parliamentary career as an Independent member of the Rajya Sabha representing Karnataka, serving from April 2006 to April 2018. In April 2018, he was re-elected to the Rajya Sabha from Karnataka for a third six-year term as a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajeev_Chandrasekhar#cite_note-5)

**Political Career and Ministerial Roles**

In July 2021, Rajeev was inducted into the [Second Modi ministry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Modi_ministry "Second Modi ministry") as a Minister of State. Leveraging his background as a technocrat, he was assigned key portfolios, serving concurrently as the Minister of State for the [Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Electronics_and_Information_Technology "Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology") (MeitY), the [Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Skill_Development_and_Entrepreneurship "Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship"), and the [Ministry of Jal Shakti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Jal_Shakti "Ministry of Jal Shakti"). Prior to his ministerial tenure, he served as a national spokesperson for the BJP.

In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Rajeev was fielded as the BJP candidate for the Thiruvananthapuram constituency in Kerala. In a highly competitive contest, he secured a significant vote share but lost to the incumbent MP [Shashi Tharoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor "Shashi Tharoor") by a narrow margin of 16,077 votes. Following the election, Rajeev continued to expand his political leadership in Keralam, subsequently taking on the role of state president of BJP Keralam.

In the April 2026 Kerala Legislative Assembly elections, Chandrasekhar contested from the Nemom constituency as the BJP-NDA candidate. He reclaimed the seat for the party by defeating the incumbent General Education Minister and CPI(M) candidate V. Sivankutty by a margin of 4,978 votes. Chandrasekhar secured 57,192 votes (a 40.75% vote share), overcoming both Sivankutty and Indian National Congress candidate K. S. Sabarinadhan. His vote share was the highest among all NDA candidates in the state during the 2026 elections.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajeev_Chandrasekhar#cite_note-6)

# Lok Sabha Election 2024: Shashi Tharoor vs Rajeev Chandrasekhar? High-octane poll battle likely in Thiruvananthapuram

## Fielding Chandrasekhar is part of BJP's aim at making inroads in Kerala, the state where it failed to win any seats in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections

[**Livemint**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/livemint), Written By [**Gulam Jeelani**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/gulam-jeelani)

Published 5 Mar 2024, 01:10 PM IST

[![Image 5: Prefer LM](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_google_2x.png)![Image 6](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_mint.png)Prefer Livemint on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=livemint.com)

![Image 7: Fielding Rajeev Chandrasekhar is part of BJP’s aim to make inroads in Kerala, where it had failed to win any seats in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/2024/03/05/382x214/shashi_-_rajeev_1709623691313_1709623709215.png)

Fielding Rajeev Chandrasekhar is part of BJP’s aim to make inroads in Kerala, where it had failed to win any seats in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections

Among the 34 Union Ministers whose names featured in BJP’s first list of [195 candidates](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-elections-2024-bjps-first-list-195-candidates-out-pm-modi-to-contest-from-varanasi-11709377199151.html) released last weekend was Rajeev Chandrasekhar, who has been fielded from Thiruvananthapuram, a seat in Kerala considered Congress leader Shashi Tharoor’s stronghold.

While Congress has yet to announce its candidate from the constituency, if they choose to field Tharoor again, it will be one of the high-profile contests in the upcoming [Lok Sabha elections 2024](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-polls-2024-pragya-thakur-ramesh-bhiduri-and-32-more-full-list-of-mps-replaced-in-bjps-1st-candidate-list-11709443167293.html#:~:text=Lok%20Sabha%20Polls%202024%3A%20BJP,and%20Ramesh%20Bidhuri%20also%20replaced.).

Fielding Chandrasekhar is part of BJP’s aim to make inroads in Kerala, where it had failed to win any seats in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. In one of his recent visits to Kerala, [Prime Minister Narendra Modi](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/bjp-can-achieve-a-double-digit-number-in-kerala-if-shashi-tharoor-crunches-number-ahead-of-lok-sabha-polls-2024-11709170022895.html) talked about the goal of achieving a two-digit figure in the state in the upcoming Lok Sabha 2024 polls.

Chandrasekhar, Union Minister of State for [Information Technology](https://www.livemint.com/ai/artificial-intelligence/india-to-come-up-with-ai-regulations-framework-by-june-july-this-year-rajeev-chandrasekhar-msde-11708409300377.html) and Skill Development, is a three-time Rajya Sabha member and will contest Lok Sabha polls for the first time. Tharoor, former Union Minister of State for External Affairs, has won the seat three times since 2009.

**Also Read:**[BJP can win ‘double digit’ number in Kerala if…: Shashi Tharoor crunches number ahead of Lok Sabha polls 2024](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/bjp-can-achieve-a-double-digit-number-in-kerala-if-shashi-tharoor-crunches-number-ahead-of-lok-sabha-polls-2024-11709170022895.html)

Chandrasekhar, 59, brings a technocratic background, having worked at Intel, founded [BPL Mobile](https://www.livemint.com/topic/bpl-mobile)[,](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-election-2024-shashi-tharoor-vs-rajeev-chandrasekhar-high-octane-poll-battle-likely-in-thiruvananthapuram-11709618797010.html)and later sold his stake for US $ 1.1 billion. Tharoor, 67, is a former international civil servant, an author, and a public intellectual apart from a politician.

## **Not born in Kerala**

Chandrasekhar and Tharoor are from Kerala, yet neither was born there. Chandrasekhar was born to Malayali parents in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. His ancestral home is in Kondayur in Thrissur district of Kerala. Tharoor was born in London, United Kingdom, to Chandran Tharoor and Sulekha Menon, a Malayali couple from [Palakkad](https://www.livemint.com/topic/palakkad), Kerala.

After completing his electrical engineering at Manipal Institute of Technology, Chandrasekhar studied Master’s in Computer Science at the Illinois Institute of Technology, Chicago. In 1988, he joined Intel. In 1991, Chandrasekhar returned to India and joined his father-in-law’s company, BPL Group. He founded BPL Mobile in 1994. However, in 2005, he sold his 64 percent stake in BPL Communications to Essar Group for US $1.1 billion. In 2005, Chandrasekhar founded [Jupiter Capital](https://www.livemint.com/Politics/neioo7F41yreW4ZWekPTzM/Jupiter-gets-Vijaydurg-project.html)[](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-election-2024-shashi-tharoor-vs-rajeev-chandrasekhar-high-octane-poll-battle-likely-in-thiruvananthapuram-11709618797010.html)with an initial investment of US$100 million.

Tharoor studied at Montfort School, Yercaud, near Salem in Tamil Nadu, and Campion School in Mumbai. He did his Bachelor’s in history from St Stephen’s College, New Delhi. Tharoor got his Master’s in International Relations from the[Fletcher School of Law](https://fletcher.tufts.edu/) and Diplomacy at Tufts University in Medford, United States. He also has a Master of Arts in Law and Diplomacy and a PhD in International Relations and Affairs.

**Also Read:**[BJP candidate list 2024: Rajya Sabha route? Not any more for these 7 Union ministers. Details here](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/bjp-candidate-list-2024-rajya-sabha-route-not-any-more-for-these-7-ministers-details-here-11709397797890.html)

Tharoor’s career in the United Nations began in 1978 as a staff member of the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Geneva. Tharoor resigned from the post of Under-Secretary-General in April 2007. In 2006, the Union government nominated Tharoor for the post of [UN Secretary-General](https://www.hindustantimes.com/india/lack-of-political-experience-no-hindrance-tharoor/story-YRIgpdDiBJM8st4FNO3bZJ.html). Tharoor finished second, behind [Ban Ki-moon](https://www.livemint.com/authors/ban-ki-moon) of South Korea.

## **Political Journey**

Chandrasekhar began his parliamentary journey in 2006 as an independent member of the Rajya Sabha, representing Karnataka. In 2018, he was re-elected for the third term to Rajya Sabha as a BJP member.

Chandrasekhar became a Minister of State following the cabinet reshuffle in July 2021 in the second [Narendra Modi government](https://www.livemint.com/topic/narendra-modi). He has been a prominent voice in the Narendra Modi government and is also present at the BJP headquarters during the induction of new leaders into the party.

Tharoor contested his first Lok Sabha elections from Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, in 2009. He won by a margin of nearly 1 lakh votes. In 2014, when Tharoor was up against [BJP veteran O Rajagopal](https://www.livemint.com/Politics/Tz5jlG9EiZzZ58UNfpk9JJ/O-Rajagopal-BJPs-first-Kerala-MLA-looks-to-change-old-noti.html), the winning margin came down to 15,470 votes. In 2019, Tharoor once again defeated BJP candidate Kummanam Rajasekharan.

**Also Read:**[Indian national from Kerala killed in anti-tank missile attack near Israel, 2 injured](https://www.livemint.com/news/india/indian-national-from-kerala-killed-in-anti-tank-missile-attack-near-israel-11709605076002.html)

Tharoor was the country’s most-followed politician on X (formerly Twitter) until 2013, when he was overtaken by Narendra Modi, the then BJP’s prime ministerial candidate. Tharoor has been Minister of State for External Affairs and [HRD](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/modi-ka-parivar-from-chai-pe-charcha-to-main-bhi-chowkidar-how-bjp-weaponises-opposition-jibes-at-pm-modi-11709609923402.html) (now Education) in the UPA governments under Prime Minister [Manmohan Singh](https://www.livemint.com/opinion/online-views/former-pm-manmohan-singh-at-91-an-inspiring-life-11695913830550.html#:~:text=In%20the%201980s%2C%20he%20was,Prime%20Minister%20for%20a%20decade.). In 2022, Tharoor lost the [Congress](https://www.livemint.com/news/i-believe-revival-of-congress-shashi-tharoor-statement-losing-congress-presidential-election-mallikarjun-kharge-11666170238297.html) presidential elections to Mallikarjun Kharge.

In December last year, Tharoor hinted that the upcoming 2024 Lok Sabha elections may mark his [final contest](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha-polls-2024/story/shashi-tharoor-hints-last-election-thiruvananthapuram-retirement-buzz-congress-bjp-future-possibilities-2481474-2023-12-28) from the Thiruvananthapuram seat. The Congress party has not announced its candidates yet.

# Lok Sabha Election 2024: Shashi Tharoor vs Rajeev Chandrasekhar? High-octane poll battle likely in Thiruvananthapuram

## Fielding Chandrasekhar is part of BJP's aim at making inroads in Kerala, the state where it failed to win any seats in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections

[**Livemint**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/livemint), Written By [**Gulam Jeelani**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/gulam-jeelani)

Published 5 Mar 2024, 01:10 PM IST

[![Image 5: Prefer LM](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_google_2x.png)![Image 6](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_mint.png)Prefer Livemint on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=livemint.com)

![Image 7: Fielding Rajeev Chandrasekhar is part of BJP’s aim to make inroads in Kerala, where it had failed to win any seats in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/2024/03/05/382x214/shashi_-_rajeev_1709623691313_1709623709215.png)

Fielding Rajeev Chandrasekhar is part of BJP’s aim to make inroads in Kerala, where it had failed to win any seats in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections

Among the 34 Union Ministers whose names featured in BJP’s first list of [195 candidates](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-elections-2024-bjps-first-list-195-candidates-out-pm-modi-to-contest-from-varanasi-11709377199151.html) released last weekend was Rajeev Chandrasekhar, who has been fielded from Thiruvananthapuram, a seat in Kerala considered Congress leader Shashi Tharoor’s stronghold.

While Congress has yet to announce its candidate from the constituency, if they choose to field Tharoor again, it will be one of the high-profile contests in the upcoming [Lok Sabha elections 2024](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-polls-2024-pragya-thakur-ramesh-bhiduri-and-32-more-full-list-of-mps-replaced-in-bjps-1st-candidate-list-11709443167293.html#:~:text=Lok%20Sabha%20Polls%202024%3A%20BJP,and%20Ramesh%20Bidhuri%20also%20replaced.).

Fielding Chandrasekhar is part of BJP’s aim to make inroads in Kerala, where it had failed to win any seats in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. In one of his recent visits to Kerala, [Prime Minister Narendra Modi](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/bjp-can-achieve-a-double-digit-number-in-kerala-if-shashi-tharoor-crunches-number-ahead-of-lok-sabha-polls-2024-11709170022895.html) talked about the goal of achieving a two-digit figure in the state in the upcoming Lok Sabha 2024 polls.

Chandrasekhar, Union Minister of State for [Information Technology](https://www.livemint.com/ai/artificial-intelligence/india-to-come-up-with-ai-regulations-framework-by-june-july-this-year-rajeev-chandrasekhar-msde-11708409300377.html) and Skill Development, is a three-time Rajya Sabha member and will contest Lok Sabha polls for the first time. Tharoor, former Union Minister of State for External Affairs, has won the seat three times since 2009.

**Also Read:**[BJP can win ‘double digit’ number in Kerala if…: Shashi Tharoor crunches number ahead of Lok Sabha polls 2024](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/bjp-can-achieve-a-double-digit-number-in-kerala-if-shashi-tharoor-crunches-number-ahead-of-lok-sabha-polls-2024-11709170022895.html)

Chandrasekhar, 59, brings a technocratic background, having worked at Intel, founded [BPL Mobile](https://www.livemint.com/topic/bpl-mobile)[,](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-election-2024-shashi-tharoor-vs-rajeev-chandrasekhar-high-octane-poll-battle-likely-in-thiruvananthapuram-11709618797010.html)and later sold his stake for US $ 1.1 billion. Tharoor, 67, is a former international civil servant, an author, and a public intellectual apart from a politician.

## **Not born in Kerala**

Chandrasekhar and Tharoor are from Kerala, yet neither was born there. Chandrasekhar was born to Malayali parents in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. His ancestral home is in Kondayur in Thrissur district of Kerala. Tharoor was born in London, United Kingdom, to Chandran Tharoor and Sulekha Menon, a Malayali couple from [Palakkad](https://www.livemint.com/topic/palakkad), Kerala.

After completing his electrical engineering at Manipal Institute of Technology, Chandrasekhar studied Master’s in Computer Science at the Illinois Institute of Technology, Chicago. In 1988, he joined Intel. In 1991, Chandrasekhar returned to India and joined his father-in-law’s company, BPL Group. He founded BPL Mobile in 1994. However, in 2005, he sold his 64 percent stake in BPL Communications to Essar Group for US $1.1 billion. In 2005, Chandrasekhar founded [Jupiter Capital](https://www.livemint.com/Politics/neioo7F41yreW4ZWekPTzM/Jupiter-gets-Vijaydurg-project.html)[](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-election-2024-shashi-tharoor-vs-rajeev-chandrasekhar-high-octane-poll-battle-likely-in-thiruvananthapuram-11709618797010.html)with an initial investment of US$100 million.

Tharoor studied at Montfort School, Yercaud, near Salem in Tamil Nadu, and Campion School in Mumbai. He did his Bachelor’s in history from St Stephen’s College, New Delhi. Tharoor got his Master’s in International Relations from the[Fletcher School of Law](https://fletcher.tufts.edu/) and Diplomacy at Tufts University in Medford, United States. He also has a Master of Arts in Law and Diplomacy and a PhD in International Relations and Affairs.

**Also Read:**[BJP candidate list 2024: Rajya Sabha route? Not any more for these 7 Union ministers. Details here](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/bjp-candidate-list-2024-rajya-sabha-route-not-any-more-for-these-7-ministers-details-here-11709397797890.html)

Tharoor’s career in the United Nations began in 1978 as a staff member of the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Geneva. Tharoor resigned from the post of Under-Secretary-General in April 2007. In 2006, the Union government nominated Tharoor for the post of [UN Secretary-General](https://www.hindustantimes.com/india/lack-of-political-experience-no-hindrance-tharoor/story-YRIgpdDiBJM8st4FNO3bZJ.html). Tharoor finished second, behind [Ban Ki-moon](https://www.livemint.com/authors/ban-ki-moon) of South Korea.

## **Political Journey**

Chandrasekhar began his parliamentary journey in 2006 as an independent member of the Rajya Sabha, representing Karnataka. In 2018, he was re-elected for the third term to Rajya Sabha as a BJP member.

Chandrasekhar became a Minister of State following the cabinet reshuffle in July 2021 in the second [Narendra Modi government](https://www.livemint.com/topic/narendra-modi). He has been a prominent voice in the Narendra Modi government and is also present at the BJP headquarters during the induction of new leaders into the party.

Tharoor contested his first Lok Sabha elections from Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, in 2009. He won by a margin of nearly 1 lakh votes. In 2014, when Tharoor was up against [BJP veteran O Rajagopal](https://www.livemint.com/Politics/Tz5jlG9EiZzZ58UNfpk9JJ/O-Rajagopal-BJPs-first-Kerala-MLA-looks-to-change-old-noti.html), the winning margin came down to 15,470 votes. In 2019, Tharoor once again defeated BJP candidate Kummanam Rajasekharan.

Tharoor was the country’s most-followed politician on X (formerly Twitter) until 2013, when he was overtaken by Narendra Modi, the then BJP’s prime ministerial candidate. Tharoor has been Minister of State for External Affairs and [HRD](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/modi-ka-parivar-from-chai-pe-charcha-to-main-bhi-chowkidar-how-bjp-weaponises-opposition-jibes-at-pm-modi-11709609923402.html) (now Education) in the UPA governments under Prime Minister [Manmohan Singh](https://www.livemint.com/opinion/online-views/former-pm-manmohan-singh-at-91-an-inspiring-life-11695913830550.html#:~:text=In%20the%201980s%2C%20he%20was,Prime%20Minister%20for%20a%20decade.). In 2022, Tharoor lost the [Congress](https://www.livemint.com/news/i-believe-revival-of-congress-shashi-tharoor-statement-losing-congress-presidential-election-mallikarjun-kharge-11666170238297.html) presidential elections to Mallikarjun Kharge.

In December last year, Tharoor hinted that the upcoming 2024 Lok Sabha elections may mark his [final contest](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha-polls-2024/story/shashi-tharoor-hints-last-election-thiruvananthapuram-retirement-buzz-congress-bjp-future-possibilities-2481474-2023-12-28) from the Thiruvananthapuram seat. The Congress party has not announced its candidates yet.

# Lok Sabha Election 2024: Shashi Tharoor vs Rajeev Chandrasekhar? High-octane poll battle likely in Thiruvananthapuram

## Fielding Chandrasekhar is part of BJP's aim at making inroads in Kerala, the state where it failed to win any seats in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections

[**Livemint**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/livemint), Written By [**Gulam Jeelani**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/gulam-jeelani)

Published 5 Mar 2024, 01:10 PM IST

[![Image 5: Prefer LM](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_google_2x.png)![Image 6](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_mint.png)Prefer Livemint on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=livemint.com)

![Image 7: Fielding Rajeev Chandrasekhar is part of BJP’s aim to make inroads in Kerala, where it had failed to win any seats in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/2024/03/05/382x214/shashi_-_rajeev_1709623691313_1709623709215.png)

Fielding Rajeev Chandrasekhar is part of BJP’s aim to make inroads in Kerala, where it had failed to win any seats in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections

Among the 34 Union Ministers whose names featured in BJP’s first list of [195 candidates](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-elections-2024-bjps-first-list-195-candidates-out-pm-modi-to-contest-from-varanasi-11709377199151.html) released last weekend was Rajeev Chandrasekhar, who has been fielded from Thiruvananthapuram, a seat in Kerala considered Congress leader Shashi Tharoor’s stronghold.

While Congress has yet to announce its candidate from the constituency, if they choose to field Tharoor again, it will be one of the high-profile contests in the upcoming [Lok Sabha elections 2024](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-polls-2024-pragya-thakur-ramesh-bhiduri-and-32-more-full-list-of-mps-replaced-in-bjps-1st-candidate-list-11709443167293.html#:~:text=Lok%20Sabha%20Polls%202024%3A%20BJP,and%20Ramesh%20Bidhuri%20also%20replaced.).

Fielding Chandrasekhar is part of BJP’s aim to make inroads in Kerala, where it had failed to win any seats in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. In one of his recent visits to Kerala, [Prime Minister Narendra Modi](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/bjp-can-achieve-a-double-digit-number-in-kerala-if-shashi-tharoor-crunches-number-ahead-of-lok-sabha-polls-2024-11709170022895.html) talked about the goal of achieving a two-digit figure in the state in the upcoming Lok Sabha 2024 polls.

Chandrasekhar, Union Minister of State for [Information Technology](https://www.livemint.com/ai/artificial-intelligence/india-to-come-up-with-ai-regulations-framework-by-june-july-this-year-rajeev-chandrasekhar-msde-11708409300377.html) and Skill Development, is a three-time Rajya Sabha member and will contest Lok Sabha polls for the first time. Tharoor, former Union Minister of State for External Affairs, has won the seat three times since 2009.

**Also Read:**[BJP can win ‘double digit’ number in Kerala if…: Shashi Tharoor crunches number ahead of Lok Sabha polls 2024](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/bjp-can-achieve-a-double-digit-number-in-kerala-if-shashi-tharoor-crunches-number-ahead-of-lok-sabha-polls-2024-11709170022895.html)

Chandrasekhar, 59, brings a technocratic background, having worked at Intel, founded [BPL Mobile](https://www.livemint.com/topic/bpl-mobile)[,](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-election-2024-shashi-tharoor-vs-rajeev-chandrasekhar-high-octane-poll-battle-likely-in-thiruvananthapuram-11709618797010.html)and later sold his stake for US $ 1.1 billion. Tharoor, 67, is a former international civil servant, an author, and a public intellectual apart from a politician.

## **Not born in Kerala**

Chandrasekhar and Tharoor are from Kerala, yet neither was born there. Chandrasekhar was born to Malayali parents in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. His ancestral home is in Kondayur in Thrissur district of Kerala. Tharoor was born in London, United Kingdom, to Chandran Tharoor and Sulekha Menon, a Malayali couple from [Palakkad](https://www.livemint.com/topic/palakkad), Kerala.

After completing his electrical engineering at Manipal Institute of Technology, Chandrasekhar studied Master’s in Computer Science at the Illinois Institute of Technology, Chicago. In 1988, he joined Intel. In 1991, Chandrasekhar returned to India and joined his father-in-law’s company, BPL Group. He founded BPL Mobile in 1994. However, in 2005, he sold his 64 percent stake in BPL Communications to Essar Group for US $1.1 billion. In 2005, Chandrasekhar founded [Jupiter Capital](https://www.livemint.com/Politics/neioo7F41yreW4ZWekPTzM/Jupiter-gets-Vijaydurg-project.html)[](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-election-2024-shashi-tharoor-vs-rajeev-chandrasekhar-high-octane-poll-battle-likely-in-thiruvananthapuram-11709618797010.html)with an initial investment of US$100 million.

Tharoor studied at Montfort School, Yercaud, near Salem in Tamil Nadu, and Campion School in Mumbai. He did his Bachelor’s in history from St Stephen’s College, New Delhi. Tharoor got his Master’s in International Relations from the[Fletcher School of Law](https://fletcher.tufts.edu/) and Diplomacy at Tufts University in Medford, United States. He also has a Master of Arts in Law and Diplomacy and a PhD in International Relations and Affairs.

**Also Read:**[BJP candidate list 2024: Rajya Sabha route? Not any more for these 7 Union ministers. Details here](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/bjp-candidate-list-2024-rajya-sabha-route-not-any-more-for-these-7-ministers-details-here-11709397797890.html)

Tharoor’s career in the United Nations began in 1978 as a staff member of the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Geneva. Tharoor resigned from the post of Under-Secretary-General in April 2007. In 2006, the Union government nominated Tharoor for the post of [UN Secretary-General](https://www.hindustantimes.com/india/lack-of-political-experience-no-hindrance-tharoor/story-YRIgpdDiBJM8st4FNO3bZJ.html). Tharoor finished second, behind [Ban Ki-moon](https://www.livemint.com/authors/ban-ki-moon) of South Korea.

## **Political Journey**

Chandrasekhar began his parliamentary journey in 2006 as an independent member of the Rajya Sabha, representing Karnataka. In 2018, he was re-elected for the third term to Rajya Sabha as a BJP member.

Chandrasekhar became a Minister of State following the cabinet reshuffle in July 2021 in the second [Narendra Modi government](https://www.livemint.com/topic/narendra-modi). He has been a prominent voice in the Narendra Modi government and is also present at the BJP headquarters during the induction of new leaders into the party.

Tharoor contested his first Lok Sabha elections from Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, in 2009. He won by a margin of nearly 1 lakh votes. In 2014, when Tharoor was up against [BJP veteran O Rajagopal](https://www.livemint.com/Politics/Tz5jlG9EiZzZ58UNfpk9JJ/O-Rajagopal-BJPs-first-Kerala-MLA-looks-to-change-old-noti.html), the winning margin came down to 15,470 votes. In 2019, Tharoor once again defeated BJP candidate Kummanam Rajasekharan.

**Also Read:**[Indian national from Kerala killed in anti-tank missile attack near Israel, 2 injured](https://www.livemint.com/news/india/indian-national-from-kerala-killed-in-anti-tank-missile-attack-near-israel-11709605076002.html)

Tharoor was the country’s most-followed politician on X (formerly Twitter) until 2013, when he was overtaken by Narendra Modi, the then BJP’s prime ministerial candidate. Tharoor has been Minister of State for External Affairs and [HRD](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/modi-ka-parivar-from-chai-pe-charcha-to-main-bhi-chowkidar-how-bjp-weaponises-opposition-jibes-at-pm-modi-11709609923402.html) (now Education) in the UPA governments under Prime Minister [Manmohan Singh](https://www.livemint.com/opinion/online-views/former-pm-manmohan-singh-at-91-an-inspiring-life-11695913830550.html#:~:text=In%20the%201980s%2C%20he%20was,Prime%20Minister%20for%20a%20decade.). In 2022, Tharoor lost the [Congress](https://www.livemint.com/news/i-believe-revival-of-congress-shashi-tharoor-statement-losing-congress-presidential-election-mallikarjun-kharge-11666170238297.html) presidential elections to Mallikarjun Kharge.

In December last year, Tharoor hinted that the upcoming 2024 Lok Sabha elections may mark his [final contest](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha-polls-2024/story/shashi-tharoor-hints-last-election-thiruvananthapuram-retirement-buzz-congress-bjp-future-possibilities-2481474-2023-12-28) from the Thiruvananthapuram seat. The Congress party has not announced its candidates yet.

# ‘If Chandrasekhar ignores the demand…’: Shashi Tharoor warns BJP leader after legal notice on defamation

## Congress leader Shashi Tharoor has replied to Union Minister, Rajeev Chandrashekhar after the latter had sent a legal defamation notice against the former.

[**Livemint**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/livemint)

Published 12 Apr 2024, 08:18 AM IST

[![Image 5: Prefer LM](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_google_2x.png)![Image 6](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_mint.png)Prefer Livemint on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=livemint.com)

![Image 7: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor responds to Union IT minister Rajeev Chandrashekhar'](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/2024/04/12/382x214/PTI03-24-2024-000079A-0_1712888890045_1712888892481.jpg)

Congress leader Shashi Tharoor responds to Union IT minister Rajeev Chandrashekhar'**(PTI)**

Congress leader Shashi Tharoor has responded to Union Minister Rajeev Chandrashekhar's defamation notice. The Congress MP from Thiruvananthapuram has denied making false allegations against the BJP leader and has demanded withdrawal of statements and apology. Tharoor has also warned of legal action if his demands get ignored.

On Thursday, Chandrasekar sent a legal notice to Shashi Tharoor, accusing him of making defamatory statements against him on a TV channel recently, alleging that Rajeev indulged in illegal activities and offered money to voters. He also alleged that Tharoor said that Chandrashekhar "is spreading lies among Christian communities."

[_'Shashi Tharoor, in desperation...': Rajeev Chandrasekhar on defamation notice to Congress MP_](https://www.livemint.com/elections/rajeev-chandrasekhar-defamation-notice-to-shashi-tharoor-congress-bjp-thiruvananthapuram-lok-sabha-elections-2024-kerala-11712738080029.html)

Following this Tharoor's lawyer stated that, "he is not responsible" for "any other versions of the same program" or any editing, post-production changes, studio recordings of casual talks, chats, or any other acts that are not intended for broadcasting.

"My client is not responsible for any 'slander' as he has not uttered any. Your client is cooking up controversies to deflect people's attention from his shortcomings and insufficiencies and to mislead their attention to couched up controversies, in his desperate bid to cause a dent on the popularity and acceptability of my client", the statement read.

[_Shashi Tharoor accepts Rajeev Chandrasekhar's challenge for open debate_](https://www.livemint.com/politics/lok-sabha-elections-2024-shashi-tharoor-accepts-rajeev-chandrasekhars-challenge-for-open-debate-11712548358279.html)

Earlier, Rajeev Chandrasekhar had said that if anybody tells lies about him, he will not remain quiet and will use all the tools under the purview of law to ensure that person is held accountable.

[_Rajeev Chandrasekhar filed ‘false affidavit’? Complainant says he is billionaire_](https://www.livemint.com/news/india/rajeev-chandrasekhar-filed-false-affidavit-with-rs-36-crore-petitioner-claims-he-is-a-billionaire-11712309994933.html)

Bharatiya Janata Party candidate Rajeev Chandrashekhar has been pitted against three-time MP Shashi Tharoor from Kerala's Thiruvananthapuram constituency.

Kerala, which sends 20 parliamentarians to the Lok Sabha will go to polls on April 26. The counting of votes will take place on June 4.

# ‘If Chandrasekhar ignores the demand…’: Shashi Tharoor warns BJP leader after legal notice on defamation

## Congress leader Shashi Tharoor has replied to Union Minister, Rajeev Chandrashekhar after the latter had sent a legal defamation notice against the former.

[**Livemint**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/livemint)

Published 12 Apr 2024, 08:18 AM IST

[![Image 5: Prefer LM](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_google_2x.png)![Image 6](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_mint.png)Prefer Livemint on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=livemint.com)

![Image 7: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor responds to Union IT minister Rajeev Chandrashekhar'](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/2024/04/12/382x214/PTI03-24-2024-000079A-0_1712888890045_1712888892481.jpg)

Congress leader Shashi Tharoor responds to Union IT minister Rajeev Chandrashekhar'**(PTI)**

Congress leader Shashi Tharoor has responded to Union Minister Rajeev Chandrashekhar's defamation notice. The Congress MP from Thiruvananthapuram has denied making false allegations against the BJP leader and has demanded withdrawal of statements and apology. Tharoor has also warned of legal action if his demands get ignored.

On Thursday, Chandrasekar sent a legal notice to Shashi Tharoor, accusing him of making defamatory statements against him on a TV channel recently, alleging that Rajeev indulged in illegal activities and offered money to voters. He also alleged that Tharoor said that Chandrashekhar "is spreading lies among Christian communities."

[_'Shashi Tharoor, in desperation...': Rajeev Chandrasekhar on defamation notice to Congress MP_](https://www.livemint.com/elections/rajeev-chandrasekhar-defamation-notice-to-shashi-tharoor-congress-bjp-thiruvananthapuram-lok-sabha-elections-2024-kerala-11712738080029.html)

Following this Tharoor's lawyer stated that, "he is not responsible" for "any other versions of the same program" or any editing, post-production changes, studio recordings of casual talks, chats, or any other acts that are not intended for broadcasting.

"My client is not responsible for any 'slander' as he has not uttered any. Your client is cooking up controversies to deflect people's attention from his shortcomings and insufficiencies and to mislead their attention to couched up controversies, in his desperate bid to cause a dent on the popularity and acceptability of my client", the statement read.

[_Shashi Tharoor accepts Rajeev Chandrasekhar's challenge for open debate_](https://www.livemint.com/politics/lok-sabha-elections-2024-shashi-tharoor-accepts-rajeev-chandrasekhars-challenge-for-open-debate-11712548358279.html)

Earlier, Rajeev Chandrasekhar had said that if anybody tells lies about him, he will not remain quiet and will use all the tools under the purview of law to ensure that person is held accountable.

[_Rajeev Chandrasekhar filed ‘false affidavit’? Complainant says he is billionaire_](https://www.livemint.com/news/india/rajeev-chandrasekhar-filed-false-affidavit-with-rs-36-crore-petitioner-claims-he-is-a-billionaire-11712309994933.html)

Bharatiya Janata Party candidate Rajeev Chandrashekhar has been pitted against three-time MP Shashi Tharoor from Kerala's Thiruvananthapuram constituency.

Kerala, which sends 20 parliamentarians to the Lok Sabha will go to polls on April 26. The counting of votes will take place on June 4.

# ‘If Chandrasekhar ignores the demand…’: Shashi Tharoor warns BJP leader after legal notice on defamation

## Congress leader Shashi Tharoor has replied to Union Minister, Rajeev Chandrashekhar after the latter had sent a legal defamation notice against the former.

[**Livemint**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/livemint)

Published 12 Apr 2024, 08:18 AM IST

[![Image 5: Prefer LM](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_google_2x.png)![Image 6](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_mint.png)Prefer Livemint on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=livemint.com)

![Image 7: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor responds to Union IT minister Rajeev Chandrashekhar'](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/2024/04/12/382x214/PTI03-24-2024-000079A-0_1712888890045_1712888892481.jpg)

Congress leader Shashi Tharoor responds to Union IT minister Rajeev Chandrashekhar'**(PTI)**

Congress leader Shashi Tharoor has responded to Union Minister Rajeev Chandrashekhar's defamation notice. The Congress MP from Thiruvananthapuram has denied making false allegations against the BJP leader and has demanded withdrawal of statements and apology. Tharoor has also warned of legal action if his demands get ignored.

On Thursday, Chandrasekar sent a legal notice to Shashi Tharoor, accusing him of making defamatory statements against him on a TV channel recently, alleging that Rajeev indulged in illegal activities and offered money to voters. He also alleged that Tharoor said that Chandrashekhar "is spreading lies among Christian communities."

[_'Shashi Tharoor, in desperation...': Rajeev Chandrasekhar on defamation notice to Congress MP_](https://www.livemint.com/elections/rajeev-chandrasekhar-defamation-notice-to-shashi-tharoor-congress-bjp-thiruvananthapuram-lok-sabha-elections-2024-kerala-11712738080029.html)

Following this Tharoor's lawyer stated that, "he is not responsible" for "any other versions of the same program" or any editing, post-production changes, studio recordings of casual talks, chats, or any other acts that are not intended for broadcasting.

"My client is not responsible for any 'slander' as he has not uttered any. Your client is cooking up controversies to deflect people's attention from his shortcomings and insufficiencies and to mislead their attention to couched up controversies, in his desperate bid to cause a dent on the popularity and acceptability of my client", the statement read.

[_Shashi Tharoor accepts Rajeev Chandrasekhar's challenge for open debate_](https://www.livemint.com/politics/lok-sabha-elections-2024-shashi-tharoor-accepts-rajeev-chandrasekhars-challenge-for-open-debate-11712548358279.html)

Earlier, Rajeev Chandrasekhar had said that if anybody tells lies about him, he will not remain quiet and will use all the tools under the purview of law to ensure that person is held accountable.

[_Rajeev Chandrasekhar filed ‘false affidavit’? Complainant says he is billionaire_](https://www.livemint.com/news/india/rajeev-chandrasekhar-filed-false-affidavit-with-rs-36-crore-petitioner-claims-he-is-a-billionaire-11712309994933.html)

Bharatiya Janata Party candidate Rajeev Chandrashekhar has been pitted against three-time MP Shashi Tharoor from Kerala's Thiruvananthapuram constituency.

Kerala, which sends 20 parliamentarians to the Lok Sabha will go to polls on April 26. The counting of votes will take place on June 4.

# Shashi Tharoor says BJP 'strong player' in Thiruvananthapuram, but Rajeev Chandrasekhar faces 'perception battle'

## Lok Sabha Election 2024: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor says he believes that the “BJP may be ahead of the Communists this time around” in Kerala.

Written By [**Akriti Anand**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/akriti-anand)

Updated 12 Apr 2024, 05:03 PM IST

[![Image 6: Prefer LM](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_google_2x.png)![Image 7](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_mint.png)Prefer Livemint on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=livemint.com)

![Image 8: Lok Sabha Elections 2024: Union Minister and BJP candidate Rajeev Chandrasekhar with Congress candidate Shashi Tharoor during a function, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, in Thiruvananthapuram, on Monday, March 11.](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/2024/04/12/382x214/PTI03-11-2024-000298B-0_1712919368722_1712919370697.jpg)

Lok Sabha Elections 2024: Union Minister and BJP candidate Rajeev Chandrasekhar with Congress candidate Shashi Tharoor during a function, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, in Thiruvananthapuram, on Monday, March 11.**(PTI)**

Shashi Tharoor, a Congress MP and candidate from Thiruvananthapuram seat in Kerala, on Friday said "it's not surprising" that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has "turned out as a strong player" in the Lok Sabha seat.

In an interview with news agency ANI, [Tharoor](https://www.livemint.com/topic/shashi-tharoor)said that in the past two elections, the BJP had emerged as the second party in his opinion. “In the first election that I fought in 2009, I took the seat from the Communists...but thereafter, the BJP has come second.”

**ALSO READ:**[LS polls: Shashi Tharoor accepts Rajeev Chandrasekhar's challenge for open debate, 'people of Thiruvananthapuram aware…’](https://www.livemint.com/politics/lok-sabha-elections-2024-shashi-tharoor-accepts-rajeev-chandrasekhars-challenge-for-open-debate-11712548358279.html)

"It's not a surprise that they have turned out to be a strong player. The [Communist campaign has been lacklustre](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-elections-2024-will-cpim-lose-national-status-famous-party-symbol-kerala-leader-ak-balan-warns-11711474851540.html)...whereas the BJP has moved into the second position in this constituency," he said.

The Congress MP went on to say that he believes the “BJP may be ahead of the [Communists](https://www.livemint.com/Politics/E96YYWck9qvKeixOJkIRZJ/Now-Kerala-communists-take-up-religion-as-a-political-tool.html)this time around.”

"It [BJP] is taking this race seriously. Frankly, it is BJP's strongest seat in Kerala. So if they have any hope at all, it is here… We are also batting with equal vehemence and confidence," he added.

## 'BJP candidate here is facing a real perception battle'

The BJP has fielded Union Minister [Rajeev Chandrasekhar](https://www.livemint.com/elections/rajeev-chandrasekhar-defamation-notice-to-shashi-tharoor-congress-bjp-thiruvananthapuram-lok-sabha-elections-2024-kerala-11712738080029.html)as its Lok Sabha election candidate from [Thiruvananthapuram](https://www.livemint.com/news/india/if-chandrasekhar-ignores-the-demand-shashi-tharoor-warns-bjp-leader-after-legal-notice-on-defamation-11712887879952.html#:~:text=Congress%20leader%20Shashi%20Tharoor%20has%20responded%20to%20Union%20Minister%20Rajeev,withdrawal%20of%20statements%20and%20apology.)— a [stronghold of Congress' Shashi Tharoor.](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-election-2024-congress-mp-shashi-tharoor-to-contest-thiruvananthapuram-in-kerala-11709906364361.html)

Tharoor said the BJP candidate "here [Thiruvananthapuram] is facing a real perception battle because of the affidavit." He alleged that "the BJP candidate's affidavit shows that he is a billionaire who is paying less taxes than the taxi drivers".

**ALSO READ:**[Shashi Tharoor's assets value has doubled in 10 years. How rich the Congress MP is?](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/shashi-tharoors-assets-value-has-doubled-in-10-years-how-rich-the-congress-mp-is-11712305591030.html)

"So in Kerala, we pay our taxes, we don't like to see this kind of things...so he has got a different kind of challenge quite beyond the Hindutva issue and communal baggage," Tharoor told ANI.

The Congress had earlier moved the Election Commission, complaining that there was a mismatch between the actual assets of Chandrasekhar and those that he had declared in his election affidavit.

According to the affidavit filed along with the nomination papers, Chandrasekhar's total income shown in the 2022-23 Income Tax return is ₹5,59,200,

— Avani Bansal (@bansalavani) [April 5, 2024](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/%22https://twitter.com/bansalavani/status/1776127163403735345?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%22) ">while it was ₹680 for the year 2021-22.

Presenting what he stated were "facts" of the matter, Chandrasekhar posted on X: "I have ONLY been in public life for several years and my income is derived ONLY from MP/minister salary, perks, and interest/dividend from savings/investments."

"In the year 2021-2022, my taxable income was sharply reduced because of partnership (in his businesses) losses incurred during the Covid period," he said.

## ‘BJP hit the ceiling in Kerala, broke 3 promises’

Tharoor agrees that the saffron party has boosted its clout in Kerala, of late. “In Kerala, the BJP went in the last 35 years from being a 2-3 per cent party to 12-13 per cent party. That's the ceiling for communal messaging. You can't grow beyond that with that kind of message.”

The Congress leader was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's “Muslim League” remark on the Congress' manifesto.

Tharoor added that the BJP's track record in Kerala and Thiruvananthapuram “is very poor”. The party made three promises in Kerala and broke all of them, he noted.

"The BJP promised three things in Kerala — AIIMS, National University of Ayurveda and National University of Disability Studies — but broke all three promises. All we can say is — _Modi ki guarantee hai_ that whatever promises they make in Kerala they will break," he added.

# Shashi Tharoor says BJP 'strong player' in Thiruvananthapuram, but Rajeev Chandrasekhar faces 'perception battle'

Lok Sabha Elections 2024: Union Minister and BJP candidate Rajeev Chandrasekhar with Congress candidate Shashi Tharoor during a function, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, in Thiruvananthapuram, on Monday, March 11.**(PTI)**

Shashi Tharoor, a Congress MP and candidate from Thiruvananthapuram seat in Kerala, on Friday said "it's not surprising" that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has "turned out as a strong player" in the Lok Sabha seat.

In an interview with news agency ANI, [Tharoor](https://www.livemint.com/topic/shashi-tharoor)said that in the past two elections, the BJP had emerged as the second party in his opinion. “In the first election that I fought in 2009, I took the seat from the Communists...but thereafter, the BJP has come second.”

**ALSO READ:**[LS polls: Shashi Tharoor accepts Rajeev Chandrasekhar's challenge for open debate, 'people of Thiruvananthapuram aware…’](https://www.livemint.com/politics/lok-sabha-elections-2024-shashi-tharoor-accepts-rajeev-chandrasekhars-challenge-for-open-debate-11712548358279.html)

"It's not a surprise that they have turned out to be a strong player. The [Communist campaign has been lacklustre](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-elections-2024-will-cpim-lose-national-status-famous-party-symbol-kerala-leader-ak-balan-warns-11711474851540.html)...whereas the BJP has moved into the second position in this constituency," he said.

The Congress MP went on to say that he believes the “BJP may be ahead of the [Communists](https://www.livemint.com/Politics/E96YYWck9qvKeixOJkIRZJ/Now-Kerala-communists-take-up-religion-as-a-political-tool.html)this time around.”

"It [BJP] is taking this race seriously. Frankly, it is BJP's strongest seat in Kerala. So if they have any hope at all, it is here… We are also batting with equal vehemence and confidence," he added.

## 'BJP candidate here is facing a real perception battle'

The BJP has fielded Union Minister [Rajeev Chandrasekhar](https://www.livemint.com/elections/rajeev-chandrasekhar-defamation-notice-to-shashi-tharoor-congress-bjp-thiruvananthapuram-lok-sabha-elections-2024-kerala-11712738080029.html)as its Lok Sabha election candidate from [Thiruvananthapuram](https://www.livemint.com/news/india/if-chandrasekhar-ignores-the-demand-shashi-tharoor-warns-bjp-leader-after-legal-notice-on-defamation-11712887879952.html#:~:text=Congress%20leader%20Shashi%20Tharoor%20has%20responded%20to%20Union%20Minister%20Rajeev,withdrawal%20of%20statements%20and%20apology.)— a [stronghold of Congress' Shashi Tharoor.](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-election-2024-congress-mp-shashi-tharoor-to-contest-thiruvananthapuram-in-kerala-11709906364361.html)

Tharoor said the BJP candidate "here [Thiruvananthapuram] is facing a real perception battle because of the affidavit." He alleged that "the BJP candidate's affidavit shows that he is a billionaire who is paying less taxes than the taxi drivers".

**ALSO READ:**[Shashi Tharoor's assets value has doubled in 10 years. How rich the Congress MP is?](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/shashi-tharoors-assets-value-has-doubled-in-10-years-how-rich-the-congress-mp-is-11712305591030.html)

"So in Kerala, we pay our taxes, we don't like to see this kind of things...so he has got a different kind of challenge quite beyond the Hindutva issue and communal baggage," Tharoor told ANI.

The Congress had earlier moved the Election Commission, complaining that there was a mismatch between the actual assets of Chandrasekhar and those that he had declared in his election affidavit.

According to the affidavit filed along with the nomination papers, Chandrasekhar's total income shown in the 2022-23 Income Tax return is ₹5,59,200,

— Avani Bansal (@bansalavani) [April 5, 2024](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/%22https://twitter.com/bansalavani/status/1776127163403735345?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%22) ">while it was ₹680 for the year 2021-22.

Presenting what he stated were "facts" of the matter, Chandrasekhar posted on X: "I have ONLY been in public life for several years and my income is derived ONLY from MP/minister salary, perks, and interest/dividend from savings/investments."

"In the year 2021-2022, my taxable income was sharply reduced because of partnership (in his businesses) losses incurred during the Covid period," he said.

## ‘BJP hit the ceiling in Kerala, broke 3 promises’

Tharoor agrees that the saffron party has boosted its clout in Kerala, of late. “In Kerala, the BJP went in the last 35 years from being a 2-3 per cent party to 12-13 per cent party. That's the ceiling for communal messaging. You can't grow beyond that with that kind of message.”

The Congress leader was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's “Muslim League” remark on the Congress' manifesto.

Tharoor added that the BJP's track record in Kerala and Thiruvananthapuram “is very poor”. The party made three promises in Kerala and broke all of them, he noted.

"The BJP promised three things in Kerala — AIIMS, National University of Ayurveda and National University of Disability Studies — but broke all three promises. All we can say is — _Modi ki guarantee hai_ that whatever promises they make in Kerala they will break," he added.

# Shashi Tharoor says BJP 'strong player' in Thiruvananthapuram, but Rajeev Chandrasekhar faces 'perception battle'

## Lok Sabha Election 2024: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor says he believes that the “BJP may be ahead of the Communists this time around” in Kerala.

Written By [**Akriti Anand**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/akriti-anand)

Updated 12 Apr 2024, 05:03 PM IST

[![Image 6: Prefer LM](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_google_2x.png)![Image 7](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_mint.png)Prefer Livemint on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=livemint.com)

![Image 8: Lok Sabha Elections 2024: Union Minister and BJP candidate Rajeev Chandrasekhar with Congress candidate Shashi Tharoor during a function, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, in Thiruvananthapuram, on Monday, March 11.](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/2024/04/12/382x214/PTI03-11-2024-000298B-0_1712919368722_1712919370697.jpg)

Lok Sabha Elections 2024: Union Minister and BJP candidate Rajeev Chandrasekhar with Congress candidate Shashi Tharoor during a function, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, in Thiruvananthapuram, on Monday, March 11.**(PTI)**

Shashi Tharoor, a Congress MP and candidate from Thiruvananthapuram seat in Kerala, on Friday said "it's not surprising" that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has "turned out as a strong player" in the Lok Sabha seat.

In an interview with news agency ANI, [Tharoor](https://www.livemint.com/topic/shashi-tharoor)said that in the past two elections, the BJP had emerged as the second party in his opinion. “In the first election that I fought in 2009, I took the seat from the Communists...but thereafter, the BJP has come second.”

**ALSO READ:**[LS polls: Shashi Tharoor accepts Rajeev Chandrasekhar's challenge for open debate, 'people of Thiruvananthapuram aware…’](https://www.livemint.com/politics/lok-sabha-elections-2024-shashi-tharoor-accepts-rajeev-chandrasekhars-challenge-for-open-debate-11712548358279.html)

"It's not a surprise that they have turned out to be a strong player. The [Communist campaign has been lacklustre](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-elections-2024-will-cpim-lose-national-status-famous-party-symbol-kerala-leader-ak-balan-warns-11711474851540.html)...whereas the BJP has moved into the second position in this constituency," he said.

The Congress MP went on to say that he believes the “BJP may be ahead of the [Communists](https://www.livemint.com/Politics/E96YYWck9qvKeixOJkIRZJ/Now-Kerala-communists-take-up-religion-as-a-political-tool.html)this time around.”

"It [BJP] is taking this race seriously. Frankly, it is BJP's strongest seat in Kerala. So if they have any hope at all, it is here… We are also batting with equal vehemence and confidence," he added.

## 'BJP candidate here is facing a real perception battle'

The BJP has fielded Union Minister [Rajeev Chandrasekhar](https://www.livemint.com/elections/rajeev-chandrasekhar-defamation-notice-to-shashi-tharoor-congress-bjp-thiruvananthapuram-lok-sabha-elections-2024-kerala-11712738080029.html)as its Lok Sabha election candidate from [Thiruvananthapuram](https://www.livemint.com/news/india/if-chandrasekhar-ignores-the-demand-shashi-tharoor-warns-bjp-leader-after-legal-notice-on-defamation-11712887879952.html#:~:text=Congress%20leader%20Shashi%20Tharoor%20has%20responded%20to%20Union%20Minister%20Rajeev,withdrawal%20of%20statements%20and%20apology.)— a [stronghold of Congress' Shashi Tharoor.](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/lok-sabha-election-2024-congress-mp-shashi-tharoor-to-contest-thiruvananthapuram-in-kerala-11709906364361.html)

Tharoor said the BJP candidate "here [Thiruvananthapuram] is facing a real perception battle because of the affidavit." He alleged that "the BJP candidate's affidavit shows that he is a billionaire who is paying less taxes than the taxi drivers".

**ALSO READ:**[Shashi Tharoor's assets value has doubled in 10 years. How rich the Congress MP is?](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/shashi-tharoors-assets-value-has-doubled-in-10-years-how-rich-the-congress-mp-is-11712305591030.html)

"So in Kerala, we pay our taxes, we don't like to see this kind of things...so he has got a different kind of challenge quite beyond the Hindutva issue and communal baggage," Tharoor told ANI.

The Congress had earlier moved the Election Commission, complaining that there was a mismatch between the actual assets of Chandrasekhar and those that he had declared in his election affidavit.

According to the affidavit filed along with the nomination papers, Chandrasekhar's total income shown in the 2022-23 Income Tax return is ₹5,59,200,

— Avani Bansal (@bansalavani) [April 5, 2024](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/%22https://twitter.com/bansalavani/status/1776127163403735345?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%22) ">while it was ₹680 for the year 2021-22.

Presenting what he stated were "facts" of the matter, Chandrasekhar posted on X: "I have ONLY been in public life for several years and my income is derived ONLY from MP/minister salary, perks, and interest/dividend from savings/investments."

"In the year 2021-2022, my taxable income was sharply reduced because of partnership (in his businesses) losses incurred during the Covid period," he said.

## ‘BJP hit the ceiling in Kerala, broke 3 promises’

Tharoor agrees that the saffron party has boosted its clout in Kerala, of late. “In Kerala, the BJP went in the last 35 years from being a 2-3 per cent party to 12-13 per cent party. That's the ceiling for communal messaging. You can't grow beyond that with that kind of message.”

The Congress leader was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's “Muslim League” remark on the Congress' manifesto.

Tharoor added that the BJP's track record in Kerala and Thiruvananthapuram “is very poor”. The party made three promises in Kerala and broke all of them, he noted.

"The BJP promised three things in Kerala — AIIMS, National University of Ayurveda and National University of Disability Studies — but broke all three promises. All we can say is — _Modi ki guarantee hai_ that whatever promises they make in Kerala they will break," he added.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Former Governor of Mizoram

**Kummanam Rajasekharan** (born 23 December 1952) is an Indian politician from [Keralam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keralam "Keralam") who has served as the [BJP Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BJP_Kerala "BJP Kerala") Chief and also the former [governor of Mizoram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_Mizoram "List of governors of Mizoram") (2018–2019). He began his political career as an activist of [Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashtriya_Swayamsevak_Sangh "Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh") (RSS) and [Sangh Parivar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangh_Parivar "Sangh Parivar") in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") in 1970. From 2015 to 2018, he was the state president of [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") (BJP) in Kerala. He is the first BJP leader from Kerala to become the head of a state. He previously served as the administrative committee member of the [Sree Padmanabha Swamy Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sree_Padmanabha_Swamy_Temple "Sree Padmanabha Swamy Temple") Devaswom in [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram"), Kerala. He actively contested for BJP in various Loksabha and assembly elections in Kerala.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-1). Under his leadership in 2016 BJP won their first ever [MLA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_the_Legislative_Assembly_(India) "Member of the Legislative Assembly (India)") seat in the [Kerala Legislative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Legislative_Assembly "Kerala Legislative Assembly") election.

Rajasekharan worked as a journalist between 1974 and 1976, before joining the [Food Corporation of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_Corporation_of_India "Food Corporation of India"). He became a high-ranking official of the Kerala [Vishva Hindu Parishad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishva_Hindu_Parishad "Vishva Hindu Parishad") (VHP) during that time. In 1987, he resigned to become a full-time [Sangh Parivar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangh_Parivar "Sangh Parivar") worker, while being instrumental in spearheading Kerala's VHP, Kshetra Samrakshana Samiti, Balasadanams, and Ekal Vidyalayas. Rajasekharan has been the secretary of [Hindu Aikya Vedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_Aikya_Vedi "Hindu Aikya Vedi"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-2)[Sabarimala Ayyappa Seva Samajam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabarimala_Ayyappa_Seva_Samajam "Sabarimala Ayyappa Seva Samajam"), general-secretary and chairman of _[Janmabhumi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janmabhumi "Janmabhumi")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-:0-3)

In 2019, he was conferred with a [Doctor of Letters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Letters "Doctor of Letters") degree by the _Shri Jagdishprasad Jhabrmal Tibrewala University_ for honouring his contributions to the field of social work.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-:0-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-4). He is one of the Party's National Executive Members from Keralam.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kummanam_Rajasekharan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Rajasekharan was born on 23 December 1952 to Adv V. K. Ramakrishna Pillai and P. Parukkutty Amma in a Vellalar Nair subcaste in [Kummanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam "Kummanam") village of [Kottayam district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district "Kottayam district"), [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"), India.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-5) He completed his school education from Government Upper Primary School in Kummanam and [N.S.S. High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nair_Service_Society_educational_institutions "List of Nair Service Society educational institutions") in [Kottayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam "Kottayam"). He completed [pre-degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-university_course "Pre-university course") education from Baselius College, Kottayam and later joined [CMS College Kottayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CMS_College_Kottayam "CMS College Kottayam") and graduated with a [Bachelor of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") in [Botany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botany "Botany"). He then took a [postgraduate diploma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postgraduate_diploma "Postgraduate diploma") in [journalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journalism "Journalism") and began a career in journalism as sub-editor in various newspapers.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-DOB-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-9)

## Professional career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kummanam_Rajasekharan&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Professional career")]

In 1974, Rajasekharan joined _[Deepika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepika\_(newspaper) "Deepika (newspaper)")_ news-daily as sub-editor, embarking on a career in journalism. He later worked in different news-dailies such as _Rastravaartha_, _Keraladesam_, _Kerala Bhooshanam_ and _Kerala Dwani_. In 1976, he took a break from journalism and joined [Food Corporation of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_Corporation_of_India "Food Corporation of India") (FCI) as a government servant. In 1979, he became Kottayam district Secretary of [Vishva Hindu Parishad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishva_Hindu_Parishad "Vishva Hindu Parishad") (VHP) and later became its state Joint Secretary in 1981. He resigned the job from FCI in 1987 and became a _pracharak_ (full-time worker) in [Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashtriya_Swayamsevak_Sangh "Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh") (RSS).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-DOB-8)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-website-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-11)

## Political career

He came into contact with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh during his student days. In 1979, he became the district-secretary of Vishwa Hindu Parishad and later was associated with many Hindu organisations in Kerala in various capacities.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-13)

In 1983, he participated in the movement against 'Nilakkal land encroachment' and worked for 'Paliyam declaration' pronounced by prominent Hindu religious scholars.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-indianexpress.com-14) In 2012, he participated in the agitation against KGS [Aranmula International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula_International_Airport "Aranmula International Airport"). He was the Chief Patron of Aranmula Heritage Village Action Council which protested against this airport.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-15)

*   In 1981, became State Joint-Secretary of Vishwa Hindu Parishad.
*   In 1983, was appointed General-Convener of [Nilakkal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilakkal "Nilakkal") Action Council and led the mass agitation against the encroachment in [Nilakkal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilakkal "Nilakkal").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-indianexpress.com-14)
*   In 1985, became General-Secretary of Hindu Munnani (Hindu Front)
*   In 1987, he contested from Thiruvananthapuram constituency as Hindu Munnani candidate.
*   In 1988, he was appointed General-Secretary of Guruvayoor Temple Action Council and led agitation to take out Jacob Thampi from managing committee of Guruvayoor Temple.
*   In 1989, was appointed Editor of [Janmabhumi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janmabhumi "Janmabhumi") daily, [Kochi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kochi "Kochi").
*   In 1992, was designated General-Convenor of [Hindu Aikya Vedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_Aikya_Vedi "Hindu Aikya Vedi").
*   In 1996, was appointed Organising-Secretary of [Vishwa Hindu Parishad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishva_Hindu_Parishad "Vishva Hindu Parishad")
*   In 1998, was appointed General-Convener of Sivagiri Samara Sahaya Samithi to assist the agitations led by Swami Prakashananda protesting against his removal from presidency of Sivagiri Madom.
*   In 2003, led a mass agitation against the [Marad massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marad_massacre "Marad massacre").
*   In 2007, was designated as Managing Director of [Janmabhumi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janmabhumi "Janmabhumi") daily.
*   In 2009, was selected as General-Secretary of [Sabarimala Ayyappa Seva Samajam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabarimala_Ayyappa_Seva_Samajam "Sabarimala Ayyappa Seva Samajam").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-16)
*   In 2010, was appointed General-Secretary of [Hindu Aikya Vedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_Aikya_Vedi "Hindu Aikya Vedi").
*   In 2011, was appointed Chairman, [Janamabhumi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janmabhumi "Janmabhumi") daily.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-17)
*   In 2012, was appointed Chief Patron (_Mukhya Rakshadhikari_) of Aranmula Heritage Village Action Council.
*   In 2015, was appointed President, [BJP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") Kerala State Unit from 18 December.
*   In 2018, was appointed the Governor of [Mizoram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mizoram "Mizoram") on May 25.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-18) He resigned from the post on 8 March 2019.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-19)
*   In 2019, contested [Lok Sabha elections 2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Indian_general_election "2019 Indian general election") from [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Thiruvananthapuram (Lok Sabha constituency)") constituency against former Union minister [Shashi Tharoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor "Shashi Tharoor") and former state minister [C. Divakaran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._Divakaran "C. Divakaran").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-20) Tharoor emerged the winner with a margin of 99,989 votes over Rajasekharan. He secured over 3.25 lakhs.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-IT-20190524-21)
*   In October 2020, he was chosen as the representative of the [Central Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") in the Administrative Committee of [Sree Padmanabha Swamy Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sree_Padmanabha_Swamy_Temple "Sree Padmanabha Swamy Temple") in [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-22)

*   Again appointed as the Chairman of the Aranmula Heritage trust, an organization for protecting and preserving the rich culture of the famous Aranmula village in Pathanamthitta district.

### Marad massacre

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kummanam_Rajasekharan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Marad massacre")]

On the evening of 2 May 2003, a group of fishermen were attacked by a [Muslim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim "Muslim") mob armed with swords and deadly weapons with the help of local political support. Nine Hindus were killed in that attack. Many were seriously wounded.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-23) Mass protests were carried out by various Hindu organisations under the banner of the Hindu Aikya Vedi, against the violence. Kerala government decided to announce compensation for victims' families and ordered a judicial inquiry into the incident. As the General-Secretary of Hindu Aikya Vedi, RSS, Kummanam Rajasekharan helped the victims of the massacre.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-24)

## Controversies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kummanam_Rajasekharan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Controversies")]

In December 2015, Kummanam Rajasekharan made a communal statement while attending a public function that, "Vendors from other religions shouldn't be allowed in temple premises and temple committees could decide on letting vendors from other religions operate at temple premises". This led to widespread protest in the state. The [Government of Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Kerala "Government of Kerala") as well as opposition parties opposed this statement and accused that Kummanam is trying to create communal division and transform the temples to RSS offices.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-25)

In May 2017, Kummanam circulated a video in his social media account which claimed [CPI(M)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_India_(Marxist) "Communist Party of India (Marxist)") men celebrating the murder of an RSS worker. The video turned out to be a fake and a police case was registered against him.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-26)

In June 2018, just days after Kummanam was sworn in as the [Governor of Mizoram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Mizoram "Governor of Mizoram"), a campaign to remove him from the post was reportedly started by the People's Representation for Identity and Status of Mizoram (PRISM), an anti-corruption organisation turned political party. PRISM appealed to churches and political parties to expel Rajasekharan from the state, the organisation called him an "anti-secular" and a "radical Hindu leader" in the appeal letter.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-27)

In October 2020, the [Aranmula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula "Aranmula") police filed a lawsuit against Kummanam, among several others, for allegedly defrauding an individual of several lakh rupees. According to the prosecution, on the premise of making him a collaborator in a factory-unit to be established in Palakkad, the accused allegedly took ₹36 lakh from the victim.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam_Rajasekharan#cite_note-28)
