**Shashi Tharoor** (Malayalam pronunciation:[[ʃɐʃi t̪ɐɾuːr]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Malayalam "Help:IPA/Malayalam"); born 9 March 1956) is an Indian politician, civil servant, author, public intellectual, diplomat, and bureaucrat. A member of the [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress"), he has represented [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Thiruvananthapuram (Lok Sabha constituency)"), [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"), in the [Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Sabha "Lok Sabha") since 2009. He was formerly an [Under-Secretary-General of the United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under-Secretary-General_of_the_United_Nations "Under-Secretary-General of the United Nations") and ran for the office of [Secretary-General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary-General_of_the_United_Nations "Secretary-General of the United Nations") in 2006, coming second.

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Tharoor&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Shashi Tharoor was born on 9 March 1956[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-1) in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), England as Shashi Krishnan Chandrashekaran Tharoor to Chandra Shekharan Nair Tharoor and Sulekha Menon, a [Nair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nair "Nair") couple from [Palakkad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palakkad "Palakkad"), Kerala, India.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-2) Tharoor has two younger sisters, Shobha and Smitha.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-3) Despite, his mother-tongue being Malayalam, he is also fluent in French.

Tharoor's father worked in various positions in London, [Bombay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay "Bombay"), [Calcutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta "Calcutta") and [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi"), including a 25-year career (culminating as group advertising manager) for _[The Statesman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Statesman\_(India) "The Statesman (India)")_. Tharoor's parents returned to India when he was 2-years old, where he joined the [Montfort School, Yercaud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montfort_School,_Yercaud "Montfort School, Yercaud"), in 1962, subsequently moving to Bombay (now Mumbai) and studying at the [Campion School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campion_School,_Mumbai "Campion School, Mumbai") (1963–68).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-4) He spent his high school years at [St. Xavier's Collegiate School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Xavier's_Collegiate_School "St. Xavier's Collegiate School"), Calcutta (1969–71).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-5)

In 1975, Tharoor graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree in history from [St. Stephen's College, Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Stephen's_College,_Delhi "St. Stephen's College, Delhi"), where he had been president of the student union and also founded the St. Stephen's Quiz Club.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-6) Within the same year, Tharoor went to the United States to obtain an [M.A.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Arts "Master of Arts") in international relations from [The Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fletcher_School_of_Law_and_Diplomacy "The Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy") at [Tufts University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tufts_University "Tufts University") in [Medford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medford,_Massachusetts "Medford, Massachusetts"). After obtaining his M.A. in 1976, Tharoor further obtained his [Master of Arts in Law and Diplomacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Arts_in_Law_and_Diplomacy "Master of Arts in Law and Diplomacy") in 1977 and his Ph.D. in International Relations and Affairs in 1978.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-7) While he was pursuing his doctorate, Tharoor was awarded the Robert B. Stewart Prize for best student and was also the first [editor-in-chief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Editor-in-chief "Editor-in-chief") of the [Fletcher Forum of International Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fletcher_Forum_of_World_Affairs "The Fletcher Forum of World Affairs").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-8) At the age of 22, he was the youngest person to receive a doctorate in the history of the Fletcher School.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-9)

## Diplomatic career (1978–2007)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Tharoor&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Diplomatic career (1978–2007)")]

Tharoor's career in the United Nations began in 1978 as a staff member of the [UN High Commissioner for Refugees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_High_Commissioner_for_Refugees "UN High Commissioner for Refugees") (UNHCR) in [Geneva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geneva "Geneva"). From 1981 until 1984 he was head of the UNHCR office in Singapore, during the [boat people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boat_people "Boat people") crisis, leading the organisation's rescue efforts at sea and succeeding in resettling a backlog of Vietnamese refugees. He also processed Polish and Acehnese refugee cases.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-10) After a further stint at the UNHCR headquarters in Geneva, during which he became the first chairman of the staff elected by UNHCR personnel worldwide, Tharoor left UNHCR. In 1989 he was appointed special assistant to the Under-secretary-general for special political affairs, the unit that later became the [Peacekeeping Operations Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_peacekeeping "United Nations peacekeeping") in New York. Until 1996, he led the team responsible for [peacekeeping operations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Protection_Force "United Nations Protection Force") in the former [Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslavia "Yugoslavia"), spending considerable time on the ground during the [civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslav_Wars "Yugoslav Wars") there.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-12)

### UN Assistant Secretary and Under-Secretary-General

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Tharoor&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: UN Assistant Secretary and Under-Secretary-General")]

In 1996, Tharoor was appointed director of communications and special projects and executive assistant to Secretary-general [Kofi Annan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Annan "Kofi Annan"). In January 2001, Tharoor was appointed as Interim Head[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-ST_UN-13) of the Department of Public Information (DPI) at the assistant-secretary-general level.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-ST_UN-13) He was subsequently confirmed as the under-secretary-general for communications and public information (UNDPI) with effect from 1 June 2002.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-ST_UN-13) In this capacity, he was responsible for the United Nations' communications strategy, enhancing the image and effectiveness of the organisation. In 2003 the secretary-general gave him the additional responsibility of United Nations coordinator for multilingualism. During his tenure at the UNDPI, Tharoor reformed the department and undertook a number of initiatives, ranging from organizing and conducting the first-ever UN seminar on Anti Semitism, the first-ever UN seminar on [Islamophobia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamophobia "Islamophobia") after the [11 September attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/11_September_attacks "11 September attacks"), and launching an annual list of "Ten Under-Reported Stories the World Ought to Know about", which was last produced in 2008 by his successor.

On 9 February 2007, Tharoor resigned from the post of under-secretary-general and left the UN on 1 April 2007.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-16)

### 2006 campaign for Secretary-General

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Tharoor&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2006 campaign for Secretary-General")]

See also: [2006 United Nations Secretary-General selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_United_Nations_Secretary-General_selection "2006 United Nations Secretary-General selection")

In 2006, the government of India nominated Tharoor for the post of [UN Secretary General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_Secretary_General "UN Secretary General").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-17) Had he won, the 50-year-old Shashi Tharoor would have become the second-youngest secretary-general, after the 46-year-old [Dag Hammarskjöld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dag_Hammarskj%C3%B6ld "Dag Hammarskjöld").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-18) Although all previous Secretaries-General had come from small countries, Prime Minister [Manmohan Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manmohan_Singh "Manmohan Singh") and National Security Advisor [M. K. Narayanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._K._Narayanan "M. K. Narayanan") felt that Tharoor's candidacy would demonstrate India's willingness to play a larger role at the United Nations.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-open-19)

Tharoor finished second, behind [Ban Ki-moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ban_Ki-moon "Ban Ki-moon") of South Korea, in each of the four straw polls conducted by the [UN Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_Security_Council "UN Security Council").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-20) In the final round, Ban emerged as the only candidate not to be vetoed by one of the [permanent members](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permanent_members_of_the_United_Nations_Security_Council "Permanent members of the United Nations Security Council"), while Tharoor received one veto from the United States. U.S. ambassador [John Bolton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_R._Bolton "John R. Bolton") later revealed his instructions from [Condoleezza Rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condoleezza_Rice "Condoleezza Rice"): "We don't want a strong Secretary-General." Tharoor was a protégé of the independently minded Kofi Annan,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-21) and a senior American official told Tharoor that the US was determined to have "No more Kofis."[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-open-19) After the vote, Tharoor withdrew his candidacy and declined Ban Ki-moon's invitation to remain in service beyond the expiry of his term as under-secretary-general.

## Post-diplomatic career (2007–2009)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Tharoor&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Post-diplomatic career (2007–2009)")]

In February 2007, amidst speculation about his post-UN future, the Indian press reported that Tharoor might be inducted into the Council of Ministers of Prime Minister Manmohan Singh as Minister of State for External Affairs. In the same month, an American gossip blog reported that Tharoor was a finalist for the position of dean of the [USC Annenberg School for Communication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USC_Annenberg_School_for_Communication_and_Journalism "USC Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism") in Los Angeles, but he withdrew his name from consideration at the final stage.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-22) Instead, Tharoor became chairman of Dubai-based Afras Ventures,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-Rediff-23) which established the Afras Academy for Business Communication (AABC) in [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram"), Kerala, the city in which he would go on to win a record four parliamentary elections. He also spoke around the world about India and Kerala, where he spent increasing amounts of time before moving to India in October 2008.

Prior to embarking on his political career, Tharoor also served on the board of overseers of the [Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fletcher_School_of_Law_and_Diplomacy "Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy"), the board of trustees of the [Aspen Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aspen_Institute "Aspen Institute"), and the advisory boards of the [Indo-American Arts Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-American_Arts_Council "Indo-American Arts Council"), the [American India Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_India_Foundation "American India Foundation"), the [World Policy Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Policy_Journal "World Policy Journal"), the Virtue Foundation, and the human rights organisation [Breakthrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakthrough_(human_rights) "Breakthrough (human rights)").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-UNESCO-24) At the Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy in 1976, he founded and was the first chair of the editorial board of _The Fletcher Forum of World Affairs_, a journal examining issues in international relations.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-25) Tharoor was an international adviser to the [International Committee of the Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Committee_of_the_Red_Cross "International Committee of the Red Cross") in Geneva from 2008 to 2011. He served on the advisory council of the [Hague Institute for International Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hague_Institute_for_International_Justice?action=edit&redlink=1 "Hague Institute for International Justice (page does not exist)")[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-The_Hague_Institute_for_Global_Justice-26) and was elected Fellow of the [New York Institute for the Humanities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Institute_for_the_Humanities "New York Institute for the Humanities") during 1995–96.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-27) He also supported various educational causes, including as Patron of [GEMS Modern Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GEMS_Modern_Academy "GEMS Modern Academy") in [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-28)

## Political career (2009–present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Tharoor&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Political career (2009–present)")]

### In government (2009–2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Tharoor&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: In government (2009–2014)")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/The_President%2C_Shri_Pranab_Mukherjee_administering_the_oath_as_Minister_of_State_to_Dr._Shashi_Tharoor%2C_at_a_Swearing-in_Ceremony%2C_at_Rashtrapati_Bhavan%2C_in_New_Delhi_on_October_28%2C_2012.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_President,_Shri_Pranab_Mukherjee_administering_the_oath_as_Minister_of_State_to_Dr._Shashi_Tharoor,_at_a_Swearing-in_Ceremony,_at_Rashtrapati_Bhavan,_in_New_Delhi_on_October_28,_2012.jpg)

[13th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Presidents_of_India "List of Presidents of India")[President of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_India "President of India")[Pranab Mukherjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pranab_Mukherjee "Pranab Mukherjee") administering the oath as Minister of State to Shashi Tharoor at a Swearing-in Ceremony, at [Rashtrapati Bhavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashtrapati_Bhavan,_New_Delhi "Rashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi"), in New Delhi in 2012.

When Tharoor began his political career, he was approached by the Congress, the Communists, and the BJP. He chose the INC because he felt ideologically aligned with the party.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-telegraphindia.com-29) In March 2009, Tharoor contested the Indian General elections as a candidate for the Congress Party in [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency "Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha constituency"), Kerala. His opponents included P. Ramachandran Nair of the [Communist Party of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_India "Communist Party of India") (CPI), Neelalohitadasan Nadar of the [Bahujan Samaj Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahujan_Samaj_Party "Bahujan Samaj Party") (BSP), MP Gangadharan of the [Nationalist Congress Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationalist_Congress_Party "Nationalist Congress Party") (NCP), and PK Krishna Das of the [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") (BJP). Despite criticism that he was an "elite outsider",[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-30) Tharoor won the elections by a margin of 99,989. He was then selected as a minister of state in the Council of Ministers of Prime Minister Manmohan Singh. On 28 May 2009, he was sworn in as minister of state for external affairs, in charge of Africa, Latin America, and the Gulf, including the Hajj pilgrimage, and the consular, passports, and visas services of the ministry. As minister of state for external affairs, he re-established long-dormant diplomatic relationships with African nations, where his fluency in French made him popular with Francophone countries and their heads of state.

Tharoor was a pioneer in using social media as an instrument of political interaction. He was India's most-followed politician on Twitter until 2013, when he was overtaken by future prime minister [Narendra Modi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi "Narendra Modi"). Some of his Twitter posts have proved controversial in the past and were highlighted negatively by the opposition and press.

Tharoor was also the first Indian minister to visit Haiti after the devastating [2010 earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Haiti_earthquake "2010 Haiti earthquake"). He reformed the arrangements relating to the conduct of the Hajj pilgrimage. He initiated new policy-planning activities on the Indian Ocean and represented India at various global events during his 11-month tenure as minister. In April 2010, Tharoor resigned from the position as Minister of State for External Affairs following allegations that he had misused his office to get shares in an [Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League") (IPL) cricket franchise. He denied the charges and, during his resignation speech in Parliament, called for a full inquiry. In a 2014 rejoinder he defended his position: "I was never involved in a scam of any sort in the IPL- I was brought down because...[I had] antagonised some powerful political cricketing interests" and added that he had "cooperated extensively with the detailed investigation conducted by the Enforcement Directorate into the entire issue", and no wrongdoing had been found.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-31)

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Manmohan_Singh_addressing_after_unveiling_the_commemoration_plaque_of_the_offsite_Campus_of_Central_University_of_Kerala%2C_at_Thiruvananthapuram%2C_in_Kerala._The_Governor_of_Kerala%2C_Shri_Nikhil_Kumar.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Manmohan_Singh_addressing_after_unveiling_the_commemoration_plaque_of_the_offsite_Campus_of_Central_University_of_Kerala,_at_Thiruvananthapuram,_in_Kerala._The_Governor_of_Kerala,_Shri_Nikhil_Kumar.jpg)

[13th prime minister of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Prime_Ministers_of_India "List of Prime Ministers of India") Manmohan Singh with Shashi Tharoor and Chief Minister Oommen Chandy unveiling the commemoration plaque of the offsite Campus of Central University of Kerala at Thiruvananthapuram, in Kerala.

Between 2010 and 2012, Tharoor remained active in Parliament and was member-convenor of the Parliamentary Forum on Disaster Management, a member of the Standing Committee on External Affairs, of the Consultative Committee of Defence, [the Public Accounts Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Accounts_Committee "Public Accounts Committee"), and the Joint Parliamentary Committee on Telecoms. He participated in several important debates of the 15th Lok Sabha, including on the Lokpal Bill, the demand for grants of the Ministry of External Affairs and of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the black money debate, and so on. In the special debate on the 60th anniversary of the Indian Parliament, Tharoor was one of four members of the Congress Party, including party President [Sonia Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonia_Gandhi "Sonia Gandhi"), Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, and Leader of the House [Pranab Mukherjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pranab_Mukherjee "Pranab Mukherjee"), to be invited to address the Lok Sabha.

In 2012, Tharoor was re-inducted into the Union Council of Ministers by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh with the portfolio of [minister of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_state "Minister of state") for [Human Resource Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_(India) "Ministry of Education (India)"). In this role, he took special interest in the problems and challenges of [adult education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_education "Adult education"), [distance education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distance_education "Distance education") and enhancing high-quality research by academic institutions. He was responsible for the ministry's written answers to Parliament's questions and responded to oral questions on education during the Lok Sabha's Question Hour. He addressed forums and conferences on education, explained a vision of India's educational challenges in the context of the country's demographic opportunities, and stressed that education was not only a socioeconomic issue, but also a national security issue.

As Member of Parliament for [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district "Thiruvananthapuram district"), Tharoor became the first elected representative in India to issue annual reports on his work as MP, including furnishing accounts of his MPLADS expenditure. In 2012, he published a half-term report followed in 2014 by a full-term report.

He termed the opportunity as a "great honour" and a "matter of duty" as a citizen of India and said he looks forward to playing his part in leading the delegation even as his party, Congress, has frowned upon his inclusion. He asserted that only national interest is above everything else.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-55) Tharoor explicitly identified Pakistan as the principal perpetrator. He emphasized in diplomatic briefings and public statements that the attack was carried out by militants linked to Lashkar-e-Taiba, operating with Pakistan's support, and stressed that India's response targeted only terrorist infrastructure.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-58) During the delegation's visit to the [9/11 Memorial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_September_11_Memorial_&_Museum "National September 11 Memorial & Museum") in New York, Tharoor highlighted the shared experience of India and the US as victims of terrorism and called for global solidarity in holding state sponsors of terror accountable.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-60)

## Publications

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Tharoor&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Publications")]

Tharoor has been a columnist in each of India's three best-known English-language newspapers,[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-61) most recently for _[The Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hindu "The Hindu")_ (2001–2008) and in a weekly column, "Shashi on Sunday," in the _[Times of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times\_of\_India "Times of India")_ (January 2007 – December 2008). Following his resignation as Minister of State for External Affairs, he began a fortnightly column on foreign policy issues in the _[Deccan Chronicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deccan\_Chronicle "Deccan Chronicle")_. Previously he was a columnist for the _[Gentleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gentleman\_(magazine) "Gentleman (magazine)")_ magazine and the _[Indian Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian\_Express "Indian Express")_ newspaper, as well as a frequent contributor to _[Newsweek International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newsweek\_International "Newsweek International")_ and the _[International Herald Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International\_Herald\_Tribune "International Herald Tribune")_. His [op-eds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Op-eds "Op-eds") and [book reviews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_reviews "Book reviews") have appeared in _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Washington\_Post "The Washington Post")_,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-62)_[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-63) and the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_,[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-64) amongst other [papers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_newspapers "List of newspapers").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] His monthly column, "India Reawakening", distributed by [Project Syndicate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Syndicate "Project Syndicate"), appears in 80 newspapers around the world.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-65) As of 2021, Tharoor has written twenty-three books in English.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-66)

Tharoor began writing at the age of 6,[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-67) and his first published story appeared in the Sunday edition of _[The Free Press Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Free\_Press\_Journal "The Free Press Journal")_, in Mumbai at age 10.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-68) His [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II")[adventure novel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adventure_novel "Adventure novel")_Operation Bellows_ about an [RAF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Air_Force "Royal Air Force") pilot Reginald Bellows, inspired by the [Biggles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biggles "Biggles") books, was serialised in the _Junior Statesman_ starting a week before his 11th birthday.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-70)_[The Great Indian Novel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Great\_Indian\_Novel "The Great Indian Novel")_ had had 43 reprints as of October 2014, and a Silver Jubilee special edition was issued on the book's 25th anniversary in October 2014, by Viking Penguin India. _The Elephant, the Tiger and the Cellphone_ has also undergone several hardback re-prints.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-72) President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") cited Shashi Tharoor's book _India From Midnight to the Millennium_ in his speech to the Indian parliament in 2000.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-73)

Tharoor has lectured widely on India,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-74) and is often quoted for his observations,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] including, "India is not, as people keep calling it, an underdeveloped country, but rather, in the context of its history and cultural heritage, a highly developed one in an advanced state of decay."[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-75) He also coined a comparison of India's "thali" to the American "melting pot": "If America is a [melting pot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melting_pot "Melting pot"), then to me India is a [thali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thali "Thali") – a selection of sumptuous dishes in different bowls. Each tastes different, and does not necessarily mix with the next, but they belong together on the same plate, and they complement each other in making the meal a satisfying repast".[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-76)

Shashi Tharoor's non-fiction work _An Era of Darkness_, published later in the United Kingdom as _Inglorious Empire: What the British Did to India_, arose out of a [speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor's_Oxford_Union_speech "Shashi Tharoor's Oxford Union speech")[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-77) he made at the [Oxford Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_Union "Oxford Union"), was published in 2016. It has sold over 100,000 copies in hardback reprints and continues to be a bestseller in the country. The British edition rose to Number 1 in the _[London Evening Standard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London\_Evening\_Standard "London Evening Standard")_ bestseller lists. Since then, he has published two other non-fiction books: _Why I Am A Hindu_ (2018) and _The Paradoxical Prime Minister_ (2018), both of which have been published in the Indian subcontinent by the Aleph Book Company.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-79) The two books, both mega-bestsellers in India. _Why I Am a Hindu_ makes the point that it is precisely because Hindus form the majority that India has survived as a plural, secular democracy, a status that come under threat in the present world. _The Paradoxical Prime Minister_ was a critical study of the present Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the effect he has had on India, along with other questions about a leader who is reviled and worshipped in equal measure.

Victor Mallet in the _[Financial Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial\_Times "Financial Times")_ said Tharoor "wants us to understand the origins of the difficulties that confronted India" after [Indian independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Independence_Act_1947 "Indian Independence Act 1947").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-80) An article by the _[New Statesman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Statesman "New Statesman")_ said it was especially important for readers in Britain in the light of post-[Brexit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brexit "Brexit") discussions.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-81) Tharoor has called for the [British government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_the_United_Kingdom "Government of the United Kingdom") to pay "colonial [reparations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reparations_(transitional_justice) "Reparations (transitional justice)")" to India.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-82)

In September 2019, he published a new book, _The Hindu Way: An Introduction_, in line with his research into Hindu culture and ways of life of late.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-83) In 2020 he published _The New World Disorder And the Indian Imperative,_ co-authored with Samir Saran, President of the [Observer Research Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Observer_Research_Foundation "Observer Research Foundation") (ORF). The book is a crucial study on the current state of chaos in international politics and identifies India's imminent role, as a non-hegemonic global power, in scripting an equitable ethic for a new international order.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-84)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Tharoor&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Tharoor's first wife was Tilottama Mukherji, a half-[Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengalis "Bengalis") and half-[Kashmiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashmiris "Kashmiris") academic,[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-85) and the granddaughter of politician [Kailash Nath Katju](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kailash_Nath_Katju "Kailash Nath Katju").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-86) Tharoor and Mukherji had been college sweethearts and were married in 1981.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-87) After their marriage, Tilottama took her husband's last name and began teaching English at [Ngee Ann Polytechnic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngee_Ann_Polytechnic "Ngee Ann Polytechnic") and also worked as a freelance writer.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-88) Their twin sons,[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-89) Kanishk and Ishaan, were born prematurely in 1984 at the [KK Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Hospital "KK Hospital") in Singapore.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-91)[Ishaan Tharoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ishaan_Tharoor "Ishaan Tharoor") grew up in Geneva, Switzerland, and was a foreign affairs journalist at _The Washington Post_.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-92) Kanishk is a former editor at Open Democracy and is the author of the highly praised short story collection _Swimmer Among The Stars_.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-94) Tilottama is currently a professor of humanities at [New York University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University "New York University").[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-95)

Tharoor and Tilottama were divorced at some point. In 2007, Tharoor married Christa Giles, a Canadian diplomat working at the United Nations.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-96) This marriage was short-lived. Tharoor next married Dubai-based businesswoman a Kashmiri Pandit [Sunanda Pushkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunanda_Pushkar "Sunanda Pushkar") at his ancestral home in Elavanchery village in Kerala's [Palakkad district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palakkad_district "Palakkad district") on 22 August 2010. He became her third husband, and step-father to her son Shiv Menon, born of a previous marriage. On 17 January 2014, Pushkar (aged 51) died at The Leela Hotel in [Chanakyapuri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chanakyapuri "Chanakyapuri"), New Delhi, under mysterious circumstances.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-97) In May 2018, Tharoor was charged with encouraging the suicide of his wife and marital cruelty under sections 306 and 498A of the Indian Penal Code.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-98)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-99) On 18 August 2021, a court in Delhi discharged Tharoor from all the charges.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-100)

Tharoor is a vegetarian and he "abhors the idea of consuming the corpses of animals," although he claimed that he does not have a problem with those who do. He has stated that he is "very proud of being a [Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu "Hindu")" and that he's a "worshipping" and "believing Hindu". Tharoor also claims to have read a "fair amount" of the [Upanishads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upanishads "Upanishads").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-101)

In April 2019, Tharoor had an accident when praying during a [Tulabharam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulabhara "Tulabhara") ritual at a temple in Thiruvananthapuram. After being discharged, he sought a probe by the government into the incident.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor#cite_note-102)

## IPL Controversy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Tharoor&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: IPL Controversy")]

The IPL controversy related with Kochi Tuskers Kerala in 2010 involved an Indian businessman [Lalit Modi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lalit_Modi "Lalit Modi"), Tharoor, then a Union Minister and his then friend and later wife Sunanda Pushkar.

Modi, who was the founder and first chairman of the Indian Premier League (IPL) was banned by the [Board of Control for Cricket in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India") (BCCI) for life on September 25, 2013 involving many disputes arising after the Kochi Tuskers matter. The core allegations related to improper use of political coercion and that of "sweat equity". The controversy erupted when Modi publicly revealed the details as regards the ownership of the then newly awarded Kochi Tuskers franchise. He said that a 25% "free equity" of Kochi Tuskars had been allocated to Sunanda Pushkar. Modi said he would not sign this franchise agreement until the financial origins of this stake were brought on record in a clear and distinct manner.

This had resulted in massive political and sports controversy, leading to Tharoor's resignation from Union Cabinet

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

**Vasudevan Sivankutty** (born 10 November 1954) is an Indian politician and the retired Minister for General Education and Labour,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._Sivankutty#cite_note-2) Government of Kerala from 2021 to 2026. He represented the [Nemom Constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemom_(State_Assembly_constituency) "Nemom (State Assembly constituency)") in the 15th [Kerala Legislative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Legislative_Assembly "Kerala Legislative Assembly").

Sivankutty is a State Committee Member of the [Communist Party of India (Marxist)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_India_(Marxist) "Communist Party of India (Marxist)") in Kerala and the State Secretary of the [Centre of Indian Trade Unions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centre_of_Indian_Trade_Unions "Centre of Indian Trade Unions") (CITU) Kerala, and the District President of CITU, Thiruvananthapuram.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=V._Sivankutty&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Sivankutty was born on 10 November 1954 at Cheruvakkal, [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._Sivankutty#cite_note-3) as the son of activist M. Vasudevan and P. Krishnamma. After schooling, he did his [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") (B.A.) at the [Sree Narayana College, Chempazhanthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sree_Narayana_College,_Chempazhanthy "Sree Narayana College, Chempazhanthy").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._Sivankutty#cite_note-4) He then completed his [Bachelor of Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Law "Bachelor of Law") (LL.B.) from [Kerala Law Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Law_Academy "Kerala Law Academy"), [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._Sivankutty#cite_note-5) He was a member of [S.F.I.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Students'_Federation_of_India "Students' Federation of India") during his studies.

Sivankutty is married to writer, journalist, women's rights activist, and a former [Kerala Public Service Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Public_Service_Commission "Kerala Public Service Commission") (P.S.C.) member R. Parvathi Devi, who is the daughter of the Marxist theorist [P. Govinda Pillai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._Govinda_Pillai "P. Govinda Pillai").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._Sivankutty#cite_note-:0-6) The couple has a son, P. Govind Sivan, who is currently a research student[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._Sivankutty#cite_note-7) at the Manipal University. Elina George is his daughter-in-law.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._Sivankutty#cite_note-8)

## Political career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=V._Sivankutty&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Political career")]

[Video 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._Sivankutty)[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:V_SIVANKUTTY_SPEECH.ogg "Play video")Duration: 3 minutes and 5 seconds.3:05[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:V_SIVANKUTTY_SPEECH.ogg)

Kerala Education minister V SIVANKUTTY SPEECH

Sivankutty entered politics through the [Students' Federation of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Students_Federation_of_India "Students Federation of India") (SFI) and has held positions such as its District President, State President, District Secretary, State Secretary and All India Joint Secretary. From SFI, he joined the [Centre of Indian Trade Unions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centre_of_Indian_Trade_Unions "Centre of Indian Trade Unions") (CITU), and currently holds positions such as its State Secretary and District President.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._Sivankutty#cite_note-9)

He was the President of the erstwhile Ulloor Panchayat, the Mayor of [Thiruvananthapuram Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Corporation "Thiruvananthapuram Corporation"), the Joint Secretary of the All India Mayors’ Council, the MLA of Thiruvananthapuram East and then Nemom (2011 - 2016).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._Sivankutty#cite_note-10)

In the recently concluded Kerala Assembly Elections, he got defeated by BJP's [Rajeev Chandrasekhar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajeev_Chandrasekhar "Rajeev Chandrasekhar"). He was a Minister in the [Pinarayi Vijayan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinarayi_Vijayan "Pinarayi Vijayan")-led LDF cabinet, handling portfolios of [General Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_General_and_Higher_Education_(Kerala) "Department of General and Higher Education (Kerala)") and Labour.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._Sivankutty#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._Sivankutty#cite_note-12) The other departments which he previously held were Literacy Movement, Employment and Training, Skills, Rehabilitation, Factories and Boilers, Insurance Medical Service, Industrial Tribunals, and Labour Courts.

## Controversies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=V._Sivankutty&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Controversies")]

### 2015 Budget Presentation Ruckus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=V._Sivankutty&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2015 Budget Presentation Ruckus")]

The Assembly witnessed ugly scenes after the Opposition MLAs attempted to prevent the Finance Minister from presenting the budget. His photos were so familiar leading the protest with the cable, sound system and monitor. Sivankutty was the major leader who opposed and created panic in assembly. Other accused in the case are minister K T Jaleel, E P Jayarajan, C K Sadasivan, K Ajith and Kunhahamed Master.Violent legislators had toppled the Speaker’s chair and threw the microphones away. The House suffered damages worth 2 lakh in the incident. Charges against the accused include relevant section of Prevention of Destruction of Public Property Act and IPC sections 447 (criminal trespass) and 427 (mischief causing damage).

The government moved the court based on a letter filed by V. Sivankutty. Several others, including Opposition leader Ramesh Chennithala, had filed petition.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._Sivankutty#cite_note-13)

### 2023 Ambulance incident

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=V._Sivankutty&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2023 Ambulance incident")]

On 12 July 2023, a pilot vehicle in Sivankutty's convoy, driving on the wrong side of the road, crashed a police jeep onto the side of ambulance van. This led to the injury of three people (including the patient). The incident took place in Kottarakkara in Kollam district when a driver from the minister's convoy. Sivankutty reportedly stepped out of the vehicle for a few minutes, inspected van, then continued towards [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram"). The police was criticised by the victims for not intervening or filing an [FIR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_information_report "First information report").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._Sivankutty#cite_note-14)

**Aranmula** is a temple town located in [Pathanamthitta district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathanamthitta_district "Pathanamthitta district") in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"), India.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-2)

## Temples

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aranmula&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Temples")]

The [Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula_Parthasarathy_Temple "Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple") is one of the major temples in Kerala and has a great antiquity. It is one of the venerated [108 Vaishnava temples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divya_Desam "Divya Desam") in India and finds mention in Tamil classics. Spread over a vast area, the temple is on the banks of the Pampa and the whole temple complex is at a high elevation. Main idol is of Lord Krishna, who is the charioteer of warrior Arjuna in [Kurukshetra War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurukshetra_War "Kurukshetra War"). The temple has a flight of 18 steps that lead to the Eastern Tower while 57 descending steps from the Northern tower reaches the Pampa. The temple here has fine murals from the 18th century."Thanka Anki", the golden ornaments of Lord Ayyappa at Sabarimala is kept in Aranmula sri parthasarathy temple.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-3)

## Aranmula Panchayat

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aranmula&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Aranmula Panchayat")]

Shija T Toji was the president of the panchayat while N S Kumar was the vice-president from 2020 to 2025. The new president and vice-president will take charge following election in December 2025.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-4)

## Environmental Movements

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aranmula&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Environmental Movements")]

The Ministry of Civil Aviation of the Government of India has issued a letter dated 25 May 2015 withdrawing the 'in-principle' approval to the proposed Aranmula Airport Project.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-5) The Civil Aviation Ministry has also forwarded copies of the letter withdrawing the approval for the airport project to the Prime Minister's Office, Rashtrapathi Bhavan, Ministry of Home Affairs, Defence Ministry, Planning Commission, Departments of Economic Affairs and Revenue, and the Project Monitoring Group at Vigyan Bhavan in New Delhi. Prior to this, on 8 May 2015, the Ministry of Defence withdrew the No Objection Certificate (NOC) to the project. Earlier, on 28 May 2014, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) had cancelled the environment clearance granted to the project by the Union Ministry of Environment and Forests.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-6)

**Kummanam** is a village that lies on either side of river [Meenachil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenachil_River "Meenachil River").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummanam#cite_note-1) Administratively it is in [Thiruvarpu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvarpu "Thiruvarpu") and [Aymanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aymanam "Aymanam") Gramapanchayat of [Kottayam district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam_district "Kottayam district") in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") State, India. Capital town of Kottayam District is 4 km east from here. A bridge named _Thazhathangadi palam_ connects either areas beside river. Kummanam is near the tourist road from [Kumarakom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumarakom "Kumarakom") to [Thekkady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thekkady "Thekkady").

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kummanam&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

_Kummanam_ has the meaning 'gloomy forest' in [Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam "Malayalam"). The abbreviation "_Ku_" in [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit "Sanskrit") refers to anything negative and _Vanam_ refers to forest. Initially Kummanam was known as "_Kuvanam_" which later evolved into Kummanam.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kummanam&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

[Thazhathangady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thazhathangady "Thazhathangady") is an ancient river port in Kummanam. "_Thazhe_" in [Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam "Malayalam") means low and "_Angadi_" refers to market. [Arabians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabians "Arabians"), [Persians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persians "Persians"), [Romans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Rome "Ancient Rome"), [Greeks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greeks "Greeks"), [Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jews "Jews"), [Syrians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrians "Syrians") and [Egyptians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egyptians "Egyptians") travelled to this ancient port for [Spice Trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spice_Trade "Spice Trade"). [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal "Portugal") traders built houses here on the banks of River Meenachil and a church dedicated to [Saint George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_George "Saint George").

Thaliyil Kotta near Thazhathangadi was the seat of Thekkumkoor kings. _Thali_ was an administrative division and _kotta_ means fort. King [Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_Varma "Marthanda Varma") annexed [Thekkumkoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thekkumkoor "Thekkumkoor") to [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore"). _Vedipurackal_ is the place where Thekkumkoor kings kept gunpowder. _Vanchiyathu_ is the place where Thekkumkoor kings kept royal canoes. There are houses still bearing these names in Thazhathangadi.

## Festivals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kummanam&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Festivals")]

Thazathangadi hosts a [boat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boat "Boat")[race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racing "Racing") or [Vallam Kali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vallam_Kali "Vallam Kali") in August/September every year during festival of [Onam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onam "Onam"). This boat race began about one hundred years ago.

## Temples

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kummanam&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Temples")]

Elamkavu Kaali temple is in Kummanam. [Thazhathangady Juma Masjid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thazhathangady_Juma_Masjid "Thazhathangady Juma Masjid"), third oldest mosques in India is more than 1000 years old locates beside Meenachil river. Southern half of it is demolished and extended with iron pillars, aluminium sheets and [minars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minaret "Minaret") in 2012. It is famous for its richness of architecture, wood carvings and the beauty.

# Lok Sabha Elections 2024 : BJP's releases first list of 195 candidates, PM Modi to contest from Varanasi

## *   The first list of 195 candidates released in Saturday features high-profile names such as Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who will contest from Varanasi in UP, and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who will contest from Gandhinagar in Gujarat

[**Livemint**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/livemint), Written By [**Gulam Jeelani**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/gulam-jeelani)

Updated 2 Mar 2024, 07:26 PM IST

[![Image 5: Prefer LM](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_google_2x.png)![Image 6](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_mint.png)Prefer Livemint on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=livemint.com)

![Image 7:  Prime Minister Narendra Modi will contest from Varanasi seat.](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/2024/03/02/382x214/ANI-20240302139-0_1709385536790_1709386669038.jpg)

 Prime Minister Narendra Modi will contest from Varanasi seat.**(Saikat Paul)**

The Bhartiya Janata Party (BJP) released the first list of 195 candidates for the upcming Lok Sabha elections here in the national capital on March 2.

The first list of 195 candidates features high-profile names such as Prime Minister [Narendra Modi](https://www.livemint.com/topic/narendra-modi)who will again contest from Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh and Union Home Minister [Amit Shah](https://www.livemint.com/topic/amit-shah) who will contest from Gandhinagar in Gujarat.

The list, which has names of 34 Union Ministers and Ministers of State, comes days before the dates of Lok Sabha polls 2024 - to be held in April-May - are announced by the [Election Commission of India](https://www.livemint.com/topic/election-commission)(ECI). Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will contest from Lucknow while Women and Child Development Minister Smriti Irani from Amethi.

Of the 195 constituencies, 51 are from Uttar Pradesh, 20 from West Bengal and five from Delhi. The list, that includes includes names of 28 women, 47 leaders under the age of 50 and 57 members from the OBC community, was read out by BJP National General Secretary, Vinod Tawde in presence of BJP National Vice President Jay Panda.

Among other Union Ministers, Jyotiraditya Scindia has been fielded from Guna, Arjun Meghwal will contest from Bikaner, Bhupendra Yadav from Alwar and Rajeev Chandrashekhar from Kerala’s Thiruvananthapuram. Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla will contest from Kota while former Madhya Pradesh chief minister Shivraj Chouhan from Vidisha in Madhya Pradesh,

In Jammu and Kashmir, the party has repeated Union Minister Jitendra Singh and present member of parliament Jugal Kishore from Udhampur and Jammu parliamentary seats, respectively. Actor-turned politician Hema Malini will again contest from her seat Mathura in Uttar Pradesh.

_Follow all live updates on BJP's first list of candidates_[_here_](https://www.livemint.comBJP candidate list Lok Sabha 2024 LIVE Updates: PM Modi to contest Varanasi seat, Shivraj Chouhan to contest Vidhisha)

The BJP has kept 370+ seats target for the party in the upcoming polls and 400+ for the National Democratic Alliance (NDA). .

In 2019, the Lok Sabha polls were held in seven phases from April 11 to May 19 to elect the members of the 17th Lok Sabha. The result, declared on May 23, saw a landslide victory for the BJP under Prime Minister Narendra Modi with 303 seats in the 543-member House.

The speculation over the f[irst list of BJP](https://www.livemint.com/topic/lok-sabha) candidates started doing rounds after a marathon meeting of BJP's [Central Election Committee](https://www.livemint.com/politics/lok-sabha-polls-2024-from-core-group-meetings-to-seat-announcement-a-look-at-bjps-strategic-roadmap-11708823248790.html)(CEC) was held on February 29. Two sitting MPs Gautam Gambhir from East Delhi and Jayant Sinha from Hazaribagh have already opted out of Lok Sabha polls earlier in the day.

The meeting was attended by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, [BJP's national President JP Nadda](https://www.livemint.com/news/india/jp-nadda-s-tenure-as-bjp-national-president-extended-till-june-2024-11673950985006.html), Home Minister Amit Shah, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, Organisation General Secretary BL Santosh, Chief Ministers, State Presidents, n-charges, co-in charges, and election in-charges of various states.

Chief Ministers of Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan, Assam, Uttarakhand, and Goa were also present.

News](https://www.livemint.com/auto-news) # O Rajagopal: BJP's first Kerala MLA looks to change old notions about the party ## BJP's first-time victory in the Kerala assembly elections is mostly attributed to the popularity of O. Rajagopal [**Nidheesh M.K.**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/nidheesh-mk),[**Preeti Zachariah**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/preeti-zachariah) Updated 20 May 2016, 08:59 PM IST [![Image 5: Prefer LM](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_google_2x.png)![Image 6](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_mint.png)Prefer Livemint on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=livemint.com) ![Image 7: The 87-year-old veteran, who contested from the Nemom constituency in Thiruvananthapuram, beat the sitting MLA, CPM leader V. Sivankutty and will now become the first representative of the BJP in Kerala’s 140-member assembly.

Photo: AFP
](https://images.livemint.com/rf/Image-621x414/LiveMint/Period2/2016/05/21/Photos/orajagopal-kDRH--621x414@LiveMint.jpg) The 87-year-old veteran, who contested from the Nemom constituency in Thiruvananthapuram, beat the sitting MLA, CPM leader V. Sivankutty and will now become the first representative of the BJP in Kerala's 140-member assembly. Photo: AFP **Bengaluru:**It has been over half a century since former Union minister O. Rajagopal entered politics—he started off as a national executive council member in the Jana Sangh way back in 1964. The last 52 years haven’t been easy ones—he has sought the public mandate in almost 13 small and big elections for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and was referred to as the BJP’s permanent candidate in Kerala, with no success. But like a veritable phoenix, he has risen from the ashes over and over again. And it has finally paid off. The 87-year-old veteran, who contested from the Nemom constituency in Thiruvananthapuram, beat the sitting Member of the Legislative Assembly, CPM leader V. Sivankutty, by 8,671 votes and will now become the first representative of the BJP in Kerala’s 140-member assembly. Born in Palakkad, Kerala, in 1929 to O. Konhikkavu Amma and Madhavan Nair, an active worker of the pre-Independence Congress party, his early life was spent in this border district. Rajettan, as he is popularly known as, then went on to take a degree in law from Chennai and began his career as an advocate in the Palakkad district court in 1956. He joined the Jana Sangh, an offshoot of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), going on to hold the post of state general secretary and later, the state party president, according to his autobiography Jeevithamritham. Later, he named his son, an acclaimed film maker now, after Shyamaprasad Mukherjee, the founder of the Jana Sangh. The Indira Gandhi-induced Emergency, however, changed everything. Rajagopal, who was among the disillusioned young people who rebelled against the authoritarianism it instigated, soon found himself sharing a cell in Thrissur’s central jail, Viyoor, with political stalwarts such as V. Velankutty Master and E.M.S. Namboodiripad. When the split between the BJP and the Janata Party happened, he went on to become the BJP’s first Kerala unit president in 1980, holding the post till 1985. Rajagopal was elected twice—in 1992 and 1998—as Rajya Sabha MP from Madhya Pradesh and was appointed as a Union minister of state during the Vajypayee government that assumed office in 1999. He held minister of state portfolios including defence, parliamentary affairs and railways at the Centre. The second time around, the seat was supposed to be given to P. Parameshwaran, the founder and head of a Kerala-based RSS think tank called Bharatheeya Vichara Kendram. But Parameshwaran says he declined and suggested it be given to Rajagopal instead. The saffron party’s first-time victory in the state assembly elections, which has disrupted the existing bipolar contest between the Left Democratic Front and the United Democratic Front, is mostly attributed to the popularity of the man himself. “He is like a Karanavar (the eldest in a family). A saint without the robes. He never agrees to any kind of violence or wrongdoing, which we do a lot. The grievance within the party is that he is too honest for politics,” said an official associated with RSS, requesting not to be named. Though his RSS ideology is integral to his personality, in a recent interview with the Indian Express he claimed that the face of the BJP in Kerala was a very different one—cow slaughter and Bharat Mata Ki Jai do not form part of it and party workers have been asked to abstain from raising these issues. “He won’t strike you as a BJP guy when you meet him on the street,” says K. Krishnachand, a Kerala-based journalist, “He just comes across as a politician who has been here for a long time.” And he isn’t just respected by the people who share his ideology. Take Congress leader Shashi Tharoor, who beat him by a margin of 15,700 votes in the 2014 Lok Sabha elections. “He has a reputation for being a kindly, friendly and honourable gentleman, which may have helped him electorally too, since many who are not of a BJP disposition felt he deserved the seat in his farewell race after 50 years of unsuccessful efforts. He is also remarkably sprightly for his 86 years, as I can testify having seen him prostrate himself before Mata Amrithanandamayi (spiritual leader) with an athleticism and flexibility that would be the envy of someone half his age,” said Tharoor. An RSS worker remembers watching from a station platform an encounter between K. Suresh Kurup, a four-time CPM MLA from Kottayam, and Rajagopal: “He was struggling with his luggage when Kurup, noticing this, came rushing to help him. He is seen as a big brother to most people, irrespective of their political leanings.” According to Krishnachand, “We expected him to give fiery speeches on Day 1 of his campaigning. Instead, he walked into the house of V.S. Shivankutty, who had met with an accident and was bound to a wheelchair, and asked him about his health.” He said Rajagopal commanded great respect in Thiruvananthapuram, and added, “I think the public really felt sympathy for this man who has been contesting right from 1999.” Catch all the [Politics News](https://www.livemint.com/politics) and Updates on Live Mint. Rajeev Chandrashekhar says that India will have its AI regulations framework by June-July this year.

India is scheduled to come up with the first draft of the AI regulations framework by June-July this year, said Rajeev Chandrasekhar, Union Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology and Minister of State for Ministry of Jal Shakti on February 20, as per NDTV Profit.

**Also Read |**[Union Minister Rajeev Chandrasekhar reacts to Paytm controversy: 'Being FinTech doesn't absolve anybody from...'](https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/union-minister-rajeev-chandrasekhar-reacts-to-paytm-controversy-being-fintech-doesnt-absolve-anybody-11706959099596.html)

“We will exploit AI to its fullest for achieving the goals of our economic growth, ensuring that it makes a big impact on healthcare & agriculture among others," said Chandrasekhar during his discussion with Anant Goenka during the Mumbai Tech Week on February 19, as per PIB.

**Also Read |**[Rajeev Chandrasekhar on India's digital-first strategy: Innovation, R&D focus, must not be afraid of AI](https://www.livemint.com/technology/tech-news/rajeev-chandrashekar-on-indias-digital-first-strategy-innovation-r-d-focus-must-not-be-afraid-of-ai-11707206143394.html)

Further expanding on the government's stance on AI, Chandrasekhar added, “We intend to exploit AI to its fullest for achieving the goals of our economic growth, ensuring that AI makes a big impact on healthcare and drug discovery, as well as on agriculture and farmer productivity. Use cases are not about having bragging rights to compete with ChatGPT. That is not the direction we are going in. We will also go ahead and support education and there will be a focus on multiple languages of India, and multiple datasets.”

**Also Read |**[RBI action on Paytm Payments Bank: Regulatory compliance cannot be ‘optional’, says Rajeev Chandrasekhar](https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/rbi-action-on-paytm-payments-bank-regulatory-compliance-cannot-be-optional-says-rajeev-chandrasekhar-11708258649573.html)

Chandrasekhar echoed the RBI's actions against Paytm Payments Bank, stressing the importance of legal compliance and the risks faced by entrepreneurs who disregard regulations in the digital economy. He warned of "severe consequences" for non-compliance, according to a Times of India report.

**Also Read |**[How to fight the “artificial” intelligence menace](https://www.livemint.com/opinion/columns/how-to-fight-the-artificial-intelligence-menace-11707886250937.html)

"India's policy is enabling and that is the qualitative structural change that has created the momentum seen today. We have to make our talent pool global standard esp in areas such as semiconductors and AI you need the ability to research and innovate," he said, [as quoted by a Mint report earlier this month](https://www.livemint.com/technology/tech-news/rajeev-chandrashekar-on-indias-digital-first-strategy-innovation-r-d-focus-must-not-be-afraid-of-ai-11707206143394.html).

# 'Shashi Tharoor, in desperation...': Rajeev Chandrasekhar on defamation notice to Congress MP

## Rajeev Chandrasekhar accuses Shashi Tharoor of spreading false information about bribing voters and has sought retraction of allegations and public apology.

Written By [**Arshdeep kaur**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/arshdeep-kaur)

Updated 10 Apr 2024, 04:31 PM IST

[![Image 4: Prefer LM](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_google_2x.png)![Image 5](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_mint.png)Prefer Livemint on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=livemint.com)

![Image 6: File photo: Union Minister & BJP candidate Rajeev Chandrasekhar with Congress candidate Shashi Tharoor during a function, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, in Thiruvananthapuram](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/2024/04/10/382x214/PTI03-11-2024-000298B-0_1712738455199_1712738457218.jpg)

File photo: Union Minister & BJP candidate Rajeev Chandrasekhar with Congress candidate Shashi Tharoor during a function, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, in Thiruvananthapuram**(PTI)**

Union Minister Rajeev Chandrasekhar has sent a legal notice to Congress MP Shashi Tharoor, accusing him of making defamatory statements against him on a TV channel recently. In the notice, Chandrasekhar has sought Tharoor to "immediately withdraw" all the allegations made against him and tender an "unconditional public apology".

Speaking with _ANI_, the Union Minister said that the Congress leader likely made the allegations “in his desperation”.

“I think Shashi Tharoor, in his desperation, has flung a lot of allegations at me,” he said.

Chandrasekhar said Tharoor, in one of the allegations, said that the BJP leader is paying money for votes. “I have said very clearly that, I will not be drawn into this negative type of politics.”

"However, if anybody defames me and attempts to trespass into an area by telling lies about me, I will certainly not be quiet. I will certainly use all the tools under the law to ensure that that person is held accountable," he told _ANI_.

## Also read: [After Congress complaint EC directs CBDT to verify assets declared by Union Minister Rajeev Chandrasekhar](https://www.livemint.com/elections/ec-election-commission-cbdt-election-affidavit-bjp-candidate-rajeev-chandrasekar-congress-11712652210041.html)

The BJP leader also warned of “appropriate criminal and civil proceedings in a competent court of law”, if the Congress MP fails to comply with the conditions of the legal notice within 24 hours.

In the notice, Chandrasekhar has alleged that Tharoor disseminated "patently false information" regarding bribing of key voters and influential figures such as parish priests, among others, by him.

Chandrasekhar is the BJP candidate for Kerala's Thiruvananthapuram. He has been pitched against Congress MP Tharoor in the Lok Sabha elections 2024 scheduled for April 26 in the constituency.

The notice charged that Tharoor's statements were made with an intent to harm Chandrasekhar's reputation and image. “His remarks also disrespected the entire Christian community of Thiruvananthapuram and its leaders, as he had accused them of engaging in cash-for-votes activities,” it added.

## Also read: [Shashi Tharoor accepts Rajeev Chandrasekhar's challenge for open debate, 'people of Thiruvananthapuram aware…’](https://www.livemint.com/politics/lok-sabha-elections-2024-shashi-tharoor-accepts-rajeev-chandrasekhars-challenge-for-open-debate-11712548358279.html)

The Congress MP's statements were also in violation of the Model Code of Conduct (MCC).

The notice further claimed the statements were also targeted at injuring the BJP leader's election campaign and benefitting Tharoor in the elections.

## Also read: [Rajeev Chandrasekhar's family assets decline from ₹65 cr to ₹36 cr in 5 years; ₹680 taxable income in FY21-22](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/rajeev-chandrasekhars-family-assets-drop-from-65-cr-to-rs-36-cr-in-5-years-680-income-in-fy2122-11712223569099.html)

It sought Tharoor to "immediately withdraw" all the allegations made against Chandrashekhar on April 6 and tender an unconditional public apology to him in print and electronic media.

In the notice, MoS IT said the Congress MP should "cease, refrain and desist from defaming, harassing, hampering the reputation" of Chandrashekhar in the future.

(_With agency inputs_)

# LS polls: Shashi Tharoor accepts Rajeev Chandrasekhar's challenge for open debate, 'people of Thiruvananthapuram aware…’

## *   Shashi Tharoor welcomes debate on politics, development, price hike, unemployment, corruption, communalism, and progress in Thiruvananthapuram against Rajeev Chandrasekhar.

Written By [**Karishma Pranav Bhavsar**](https://www.livemint.com/authors/karishma-pranav-bhavsar)

Updated 8 Apr 2024, 10:03 AM IST

[![Image 5: Prefer LM](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_google_2x.png)![Image 6](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/flipcoin_mint.png)Prefer Livemint on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=livemint.com)

![Image 7: Shashi Tharoor is a member of the Congress Working Committee and one of the popular faces of the party in the country.](https://www.livemint.com/lm-img/img/2024/04/08/382x214/Shashi-Tharoor-is-a-member-of-the-Congress-Working_1707144161589_1712550283007.jpg)

Shashi Tharoor is a member of the Congress Working Committee and one of the popular faces of the party in the country.**(ANI)**

Shashi Tharoor, who is eyeing a fourth consecutive win from the Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha seat, on Sunday accepted the BJP candidate and Union Minister Rajeev Chandrasekhar's ‘challenge for an open debate’.

The Congress Thiruvananthapuram MP shared a clip of the Union Minister who told the local media during the poll campaign that, “I am ready to debate over ideas, development, and whose track record is better. I have been saying this since the beginning.”

On this, Tharoor wrote, “Yes, I welcome a debate. But the people of Thiruvananthapuram are aware of who has been evading a debate till now. Let us debate politics and development. Let us debate price hike, unemployment, corruption, communalism, and the BJP's 10 years of propagating politics of hatred.”

Further adding, he said, “Let us also discuss about the development of Thiruvananthapuram and the visible progress we have made in the last 15 years.”

Notably, both the leaders are contesting against each other from Thiruvananthapuram. In 2009, 2014 and 2019 Lok Sabha Elections, Tharoor has been winning from this seat.

Meanwhile, both the leaders have declared their assets. The sitting MP has d[eclared assets of over ₹55 crore](https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/shashi-tharoors-assets-value-has-doubled-in-10-years-how-rich-the-congress-mp-is-11712305591030.html) in his nomination papers while Chandrasekhar declared assets worth over ₹28 crore.

While giving details of his assets and liabilities, in the affidavit, he mentioned that he has movable assets of over ₹49 crore while immovable assets are worth over ₹6.75 crore. He also owns two cars, a Maruti Ciaz and a Maruti XL6, as per the affidavit.
