**Thiruvananthapuram district** (Malayalam:[[t̪iɾuʋɐnɐn̪d̪ɐpuɾɐm]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Malayalam "Help:IPA/Malayalam")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/8/86/En-Thiruvananthapuram.oga/En-Thiruvananthapuram.oga.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:En-Thiruvananthapuram.oga "File:En-Thiruvananthapuram.oga")) is the [southernmost district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_districts_of_Kerala "List of districts of Kerala") in the [Indian state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_union_territories_of_India "States and union territories of India") of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"). The district was created in 1949, with its headquarters in the city of [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram"), which is also Kerala's administrative centre. The present district was created in 1956 by separating the four southernmost Taluks of the erstwhile district to form [Kanyakumari district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari_district "Kanyakumari district"). The city of [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram") is also known as the [Information technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_technology "Information technology") capital of the state, since it is home to the first and largest IT park in India, [Technopark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technopark,_Trivandrum "Technopark, Trivandrum"), established in 1990. The district is home to more than 9% of total population of the state.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-8)

The district covers an area of 2,192 square kilometres (541,655 acres). At the 2011 census, it had a population of 3,301,427,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-District_population-10) making it the second most populous district in Kerala after [Malappuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malappuram_district "Malappuram district").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-districtcensus-11) Its population density is the highest in Kerala, with 1,509 inhabitants per square kilometre (3,910/sq mi).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-Kerala_Provisional_Population_Totals-12) The district is divided into six [subdistricts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil"): [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_taluk "Thiruvananthapuram taluk"), [Chirayinkeezhu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chirayinkeezhu_taluk "Chirayinkeezhu taluk"), [Neyyattinkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyattinkara_taluk "Neyyattinkara taluk"), [Nedumangadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedumangad_taluk "Nedumangad taluk"), [Varkala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala "Varkala"), and [Kattakada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattakada "Kattakada"). The urban bodies in the district are the [Thiruvananthapuram Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Municipal_Corporation "Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation"), and the [Varkala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala "Varkala"), [Neyyattinkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyattinkara "Neyyattinkara"), [Attingal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attingal "Attingal"), and [Nedumangad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedumangad "Nedumangad") municipalities.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-13)

Thiruvananthapuram district is located between [8°10′N 76°25′E / 8.17°N 76.41°E / 8.17; 76.41](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Thiruvananthapuram_district&params=8.17_N_76.41_E_) and [8°32′N 77°10′E / 8.54°N 77.17°E / 8.54; 77.17](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Thiruvananthapuram_district&params=8.54_N_77.17_E_). At the southernmost extremity of the district, Kaliyikkavila is 54 kilometres (34 mi) from [Kanyakumari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari "Kanyakumari"), the southernmost point on the Indian peninsula.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-14) 33.75% of the district population lives in urban areas.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-15)

The district has three major rivers, several freshwater lakes, and over 300 ponds. Its eastern region is forested, northern regions are mostly under rubber cultivation and the remaining areas grow mixed dry-land crops of coconut, plantain, and tapioca, among others. Built-up areas and rice fields complete the land use pattern.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-16)

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

The name Thiruvananthapuram, shared by the district and its headquarters city, comes from the [Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam "Malayalam")/[Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_language "Tamil language") word "Thiru" and [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit_language "Sanskrit language") word "anantha-pura", meaning "Abode of Lord Anantha".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-Meaning_of_name-17) The name derives from the deity of the [Hindu temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_temple "Hindu temple") at the center of Thiruvananthapuram city. Anantha is another name of Vishnu, the deity of [Sree Padmanabhaswamy temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sree_Padmanabhaswamy_temple "Sree Padmanabhaswamy temple"). The district's official name in English was Trivandrum until 1991, when the government reinstated the city's original name, Thiruvananthapuram, in all languages.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

See also: [Merger of Kanyakumari with Madras State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merger_of_Kanyakumari_with_Madras_State "Merger of Kanyakumari with Madras State")

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Kanakakkunnu_Palace_DSW.jpg/250px-Kanakakkunnu_Palace_DSW.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kanakakkunnu_Palace_DSW.jpg)

[Kanakakkunnu Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanakakkunnu_Palace "Kanakakkunnu Palace") at [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram")

The city of Thiruvananthapuram features several landmarks with regards to ancient tradition, folklore, and literature. Several other locations in the district feature similar landmarks. The [Chera dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chera_dynasty "Chera dynasty") governed the area of [Malabar Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malabar_Coast "Malabar Coast") between [Kanyakumari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari "Kanyakumari") in the south to [Kasaragod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasaragod "Kasaragod") in the north. This included [Palakkad Gap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palakkad_Gap "Palakkad Gap"), [Coimbatore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coimbatore "Coimbatore"), [Salem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salem,_Tamil_Nadu "Salem, Tamil Nadu"), and [Kolli Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolli_Hills "Kolli Hills"). The region around [Coimbatore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coimbatore "Coimbatore") served as the eastern entrance to the [Palakkad Gap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palakkad_Gap "Palakkad Gap"), the mountain pass that is the principal trade route between the [Malabar Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malabar_Coast "Malabar Coast") and [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-Trade-18) The southernmost region of present-day Malabar coast (the coastal belt between Kanyakumari and Kollam) was ruled by the [Ay dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ay_dynasty "Ay dynasty"), who were related to, and officially feudatories of the Cheras.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-19) The Ay Dynasty (later known as the Venad Dynasty and finally the Thiruvithamkur Dynasty), followed by the Nannan Dynasty (later known as the [Mushika dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushika_dynasty "Mushika dynasty") and finally the [Kolathiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolathiri "Kolathiri") dynasty), were the two oldest and most important lineages of the [Velir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velir "Velir") clan, who had very frequent intermarriages with the Cheras, [Cholas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chola_dynasty "Chola dynasty"), and the [Pandyas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandya_dynasty "Pandya dynasty").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-24)

Present-day [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram") city, district, and [Kanyakumari district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari_district "Kanyakumari district"), were ruled by the [Ay dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ay_dynasty "Ay dynasty") during ancient and medieval ages, which was a [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_language "Tamil language") kingdom based in the southernmost part of Indian Subcontinent.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-askh-25) Ay kingdom had experienced attacks and conquests by [Cholas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chola_dynasty "Chola dynasty") and [Pandyas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandya_dynasty "Pandya dynasty") in various periods.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-askh-25) Later it became a part of [Venad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venad "Venad") in late Middle Ages, which was eventually expanded as the powerful kingdom of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") in 18th century CE.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-askh-25) The [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamils "Tamils")-Dravidian kind of architecture is also found in Padmanabhaswamy temple, which makes it distinct from the architectural style of temples in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") in general.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-askh-25)

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/1733_Homann_Heirs_Map_of_India_-_Geographicus_-_India-homannheirs-1733.jpg/250px-1733_Homann_Heirs_Map_of_India_-_Geographicus_-_India-homannheirs-1733.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1733_Homann_Heirs_Map_of_India_-_Geographicus_-_India-homannheirs-1733.jpg)

A map of [Malabar Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malabar_Coast "Malabar Coast") drawn by Homann Heirs in 1733. At that time, Travancore was only a small territory wedged between [Kollam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kollam "Kollam") and [Kanyakumari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari "Kanyakumari"), as shown in the map (Present-day districts of Trivandrum and Kanyakumari only).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-:302-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-:3-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-majumdar407-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-:6-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-31)

In 1684, during the [regency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regent "Regent") of [Umayamma Rani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umayamma_Rani "Umayamma Rani"), the [English East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_East_India_Company "English East India Company") acquired a sandy spit of land at [Anchuthengu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anchuthengu "Anchuthengu"), near [Varkala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala "Varkala") on the sea coast about 32 kilometres (20 mi) north of Thiruvananthapuram city, with a view to erecting a factory and fortifying it. The location had earlier been frequented by the Dutch, then by the British. It was from here that the English gradually extended their diplomacy to other parts of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-32)

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Travancore_1871.JPG/250px-Travancore_1871.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Travancore_1871.JPG)

A map of the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj")[Princely state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_state "Princely state") of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") published in 1871

Modern history begins with [Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_Varma "Marthanda Varma") (1729 CE–1758 CE), generally regarded as the Father of modern [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore"). In the early 18th century CE, the [Travancore royal family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore_royal_family "Travancore royal family") adopted some members from the royal family of [Kolathunadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolathunadu "Kolathunadu") (a long separated younger sister dynasty of Ay/Venad/Thiruvithamkur with whom they had the tradition of mutual adoption of heirs for centuries) based in [Kannur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kannur "Kannur").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-33) Thiruvananthapuram was known as a great center of intellectual and artistic activity at this time. [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") became the most dominant state in Kerala by defeating the powerful [Zamorin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamorin "Zamorin") of [Kozhikode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Kozhikode "History of Kozhikode") in the battle of [Purakkad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purakkad "Purakkad") in 1755.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-AHoT_162-34)

The temple of Vishnu reclining on Anantha, the [Sri Padmanabhaswamy temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Padmanabhaswamy_temple "Sri Padmanabhaswamy temple"), is the most recognizable and iconic landmark of the city and the district and dates back to the times of the Azhvars, and is one among the 108 shrines mentioned in their texts. In addition to the presiding deity of [Padmanabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishnu "Vishnu"), this temple contains several shrines, dedicated to [Krishna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna "Krishna"), [Narasimha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narasimha "Narasimha") and [Ayyappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayyappa "Ayyappa"). King Marthanda Varma, after his conquest of Southern Kerala upto the Aluva, submitted the kingdom to Padmanabha and took upon the title of 'Sree Padmanabhadasa', the Servant of Sree Padmanabha. The vast temple complex, with its tall [Gopuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gopuram "Gopuram") decorated with detailed carvings reflected in a huge [temple tank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_tank "Temple tank"), is today a center of attraction for devotees and sightseers.

The city was the capital of the [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") state from 18th century CE until [India's independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_independence_movement "Indian independence movement"). The Thiruvananthapuram Municipality came into existence in 1920 as the first municipality in [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") region. After two decades, during the reign of [Sree Chithira Thirunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sree_Chithira_Thirunal "Sree Chithira Thirunal"), Thiruvananthapuram Municipality was converted into Corporation on 30 October 1940.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-35) Consequent to the recommendations of the State Reorganization Commission, the Vilavancode subdistrict of Thiruvananthapuram was merged with [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu"), along with another three southern subdistricts, Thovala, Agastheewaram, and Kalkulam from [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") which eventually formed Tamil Nadu's [Kanyakumari district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari_district "Kanyakumari district"). The state of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") came into being on 1 November 1956.

### Kilimanoor palace

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Kilimanoor palace")]

See also: [Kilimanoor palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor_palace "Kilimanoor palace")

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Studiorrv.jpg/250px-Studiorrv.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Studiorrv.jpg)

Birthplace of [Raja Ravi Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma "Raja Ravi Varma") with his studio in the foreground

In 1705 ([ME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam_era "Malayalam era") 880) the son and two daughters of Ittammar Raja of [Parappanad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parappanad "Parappanad") royal house (originally based at [Parappanangadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parappanangadi "Parappanangadi") in present-day [Malappuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malappuram_district "Malappuram district")) were adopted into the Royal house of [Venad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venad "Venad"). Ittammar Raja's sister and her sons, Rama Varma and Raghava Varma, settled in Kilimanoor and married the now adopted sisters. [Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_Varma "Marthanda Varma"), the founder of the Kingdom of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore"), was the son of Raghava Varma. The nephew[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-36) of Raghava Varma, Ravi Varma Koil Thampuran, married the sister of Marthanda Varma. Their son became known as [Dharma Raja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharma_Raja "Dharma Raja") Kartika Thirunnal Rama Varma.

In 1740 when an allied force,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-37) led by Dutchman Captain Hockert supporting the Deshinganadu King, attacked Venad, an army from Kilimanoor resisted and then defeated them. Although a small victory, this was the first time an Indian army had defeated a European power. In 1753, in recognition of this feat, Marthanda Varma exempted the areas controlled by the Kilimanoor palace[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-38) from taxes, and granted them autonomous status.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-39) The present palace complex was built at this time, together with the Ayyappa temple.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-40) for the family deity, _Sastha_ or Ayyapan.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[Velu Thampi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velu_Thampi_Dalawa "Velu Thampi Dalawa")[Dalawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewan "Dewan") held meetings at Kilimanoor palace while planning uprisings against the British. He handed over his sword at the palace before going into his final battle against the British, and India's first President, Dr [Rajendra Prasad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajendra_Prasad "Rajendra Prasad") received this sword from the palace and it was kept in the [National Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum,_New_Delhi "National Museum, New Delhi") in [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi"). Afterwards the sword was moved to the Napier Museum, Thiruvananthapuram.

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Geography")]

Main article: [Geography of Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Thiruvananthapuram "Geography of Thiruvananthapuram")

[![Image 20: A panoramic view of Varkala Beach Cliff](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/37/Panoramic_view_of_varkala_beach_cliff.jpg/1280px-Panoramic_view_of_varkala_beach_cliff.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Panoramic_view_of_varkala_beach_cliff.jpg "A panoramic view of Varkala Beach Cliff")

[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Panoramic_view_of_varkala_beach_cliff.jpg "File:Panoramic view of varkala beach cliff.jpg")

A panoramic view of [Varkala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala "Varkala") Beach [Cliff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cliff "Cliff")

The district is located between [8°10′N 76°25′E / 8.17°N 76.41°E / 8.17; 76.41](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Thiruvananthapuram_district&params=8.17_N_76.41_E_) and [8°32′N 77°10′E / 8.54°N 77.17°E / 8.54; 77.17](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Thiruvananthapuram_district&params=8.54_N_77.17_E_). The southernmost part of the city, [Parassala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parassala "Parassala"), is just 54 kilometres (34 mi) away from the southern [peninsular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peninsular "Peninsular") tip of India, [Cape Comorin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari_(town) "Kanyakumari (town)") (Kanyakumari). The district stretches 78 kilometres (48 mi) along the shores of the [Arabian Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Sea "Arabian Sea") on the west. [Kollam district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kollam_district "Kollam district") lies to the north, with the [Tirunelveli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tirunelveli_district "Tirunelveli district") and [Kanyakumari districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari_district "Kanyakumari district") of [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu") to the east and south respectively.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-41)

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Climate")]

The climate of Thiruvananthapuram district is generally hot and [tropical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropics "Tropics"). Large forest reserves have a favorable effect on the climate and induce rains. Cold weather is experienced in the [mountain ranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Ghats "Western Ghats"). Lower down, the weather is bracing, and generally hot in the coastal regions. The mean maximum temperature is 95°F (35°C) and the mean minimum temperature is 69°F (20°C). As the district stretches from north to south, with the [Arabian Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Sea "Arabian Sea") to the west, the [relative humidity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relative_humidity "Relative humidity") is generally high. It rises to about 95% during the [southwest monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon#Southwest_monsoon "Monsoon").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-42)

The total annual rainfall in the district is about 1,827.7 mm (72 in) per annum.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-43) The southwest monsoon, from June to September is the principal rainy season, during which the district receives most of its annual rainfall. The second rainy season is the [Northeast monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon#Northeast_monsoon "Monsoon"), from October to November. The district also experiences thunderstorm rains in the pre-monsoon months of April and May.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-44)

December to February are the coolest months. The average temperature drops to 69°F (20°C) in these months, generally considered India's [winter season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_of_India#winter "Climate of India"). The [summer season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_of_India#Summer "Climate of India") starts in February and continues until May. The average temperature rises to 95°F (35°C) in these months.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-45)

## Economy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Economy")]

Main article: [Economy of Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Thiruvananthapuram "Economy of Thiruvananthapuram")

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Pattom_Skyline_panoramo_02.jpg/960px-Pattom_Skyline_panoramo_02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pattom_Skyline_panoramo_02.jpg "A view of the city of Thiruvananthapuram from Pattom.")

[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pattom_Skyline_panoramo_02.jpg "File:Pattom Skyline panoramo 02.jpg")

A view of the city of [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram") from [Pattom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattom "Pattom").

The media and [information technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_technology_in_India "Information technology in India") sectors are mainstays of Thiruvananthapuram district's economy, and other major sectors are tourism and [leisure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leisure "Leisure"), agriculture, and education. India's first animation park, the [Kinfra Animation Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinfra_Film_and_Video_Park "Kinfra Film and Video Park"), is in the district.

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Technopark_Trivandum_Ganga_and_Yamuna_Buildings.jpg/250px-Technopark_Trivandum_Ganga_and_Yamuna_Buildings.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Technopark_Trivandum_Ganga_and_Yamuna_Buildings.jpg)

A [Technopark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technopark_Kerala "Technopark Kerala") building. Technopark as of 2010 has 450,000 m 2 (4,800,000 sq ft) of built-up space, and is home to over 200 companies, employing around 30,000 professionals.

Thiruvananthapuram district has 2 central-sector, 14 state-sector, 1 co-operative-sector, 4 joint-sector, and 60 private-sector medium- and large-scale enterprises. As of 31 March 2003, [Kerala State Industrial Development Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Industrial_Development_Corporation "Kerala State Industrial Development Corporation") (KSIDC) units employed 9,262 people, and had invested Rs. 3439.4 million.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-48) In 2002, there were 901 registered working factories, including oil mills, cashew factories, [Cotton mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotton_mill "Cotton mill"), [Sawmills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawmill "Sawmill"), [printing units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offset_printing "Offset printing"), rubber industrial units, chemical units, match factories, general engineering units, and automobile workshops. The Shree Mulam Thirunal Shashtiabdapoorthy Memorial Institute (S.M.S.M. Institute) in Thiruvananthapuram city is a major state government emporium marketing products of Kerala's [handicraft industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handicraft "Handicraft").

The Neyyar Irrigation Project, commissioned in 1959, irrigates an area of 116.65 km 2 (45.0 sq mi). The [Neyyar river](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyar_(river) "Neyyar (river)") is the source of water for the [Neyyar reservoir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyar_Dam "Neyyar Dam"). The dam is 294.13 metres (965.0 ft) long and 50.6 metres (166.0 ft) high. The catchment draining into the reservoir, covering an area of 140 km 2 (54 sq mi) of forest, receives an annual average rainfall of about 2,260 mm (90 in) 2260 mm from the two monsoons. The total length of the main canal and its branches is 266 km (165 mi).

### Collectorate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Collectorate")]

The headquarters of the district administration is at [Kudappanakunnu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kudappanakunnu "Kudappanakunnu"), Thiruvananthapuram. The district administration is headed by the [District collector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_collector "District collector"). He/She is assisted by five deputy collectors with responsibility for general matters, land acquisition, revenue recovery, land reforms, disaster management and elections.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-49) For revenue administration, the district is divided into two revenue divisions: Thiruvananthapuram and Nedumangad, each headed by a Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) or Sub Collector, who is also the [Sub Divisional Magistrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sub-divisional_magistrate "Sub-divisional magistrate").

**Nemom Assembly constituency** is one of the 140 [state legislative assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Legislative_Assembly "Kerala Legislative Assembly") constituencies in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"), India. It is one of the seven assembly segments that constitute the [Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency "Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha constituency").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemom_Assembly_constituency#cite_note-1) Since 2026, the constituency has been represented by [Rajeev Chandrasekhar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajeev_Chandrasekhar "Rajeev Chandrasekhar") of the [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party")

This constituency serves as a vital stronghold for the [RSS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashtriya_Swayamsevak_Sangh "Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh"), dominated by [Nair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nair "Nair") population.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemom_Assembly_constituency#cite_note-2)

## Local self-governed segments

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nemom_Assembly_constituency&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Local self-governed segments")]

Nemom is composed of 22 wards of the [Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Municipal_Corporation "Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation").

The wards are:[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemom_Assembly_constituency#cite_note-3)

1.   Thirumala
2.   Thirikkannapuram
3.   Punnakkamugal
4.   Poojappura
5.   Mudavanmugal
6.   Estate
7.   Nemom
8.   Ponnumangalam
9.   Melamcode
10.   Pappanamcode
11.   Karamana
12.   Nedumcaud
13.   Kaladi
14.   Karumom
15.   Punchakkari
16.   Poonkulam
17.   Vellar
18.   Thiruvallam
19.   Ambalathara
20.   [Attukal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attukal "Attukal")
21.   Kalippankulam
22.   Kamaleswaram

After the 2008 delimitation, major parts of previous Trivandrum East Assembly were added to Nemom.

- birthplace of a famous artist born in an aristocratic family

- the incumbent Member of Parliament from this constituency has been elected for three consecutive terms
- the city derives its current name from the name of a local deity and has a temple dedicated to that deity.

**Ahmedabad** ([/ˈ ɑː m ə d ə b æ d,-b ɑː d/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_AH-mə-də-ba(h)d_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"), Hindustani:[[ɛʱ(ɛ).m(ə).d̪ɑː.bɑːd̪]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu")), also spelt **Amdavad** (Gujarati:[[ˈəmdɑʋɑd]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Gujarati "Help:IPA/Gujarati")) and historically known as **Karnavati** (Sanskrit:[[kɐrɳaːʋɐt̪iː]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Sanskrit "Help:IPA/Sanskrit")), is the most populous city in the Indian [state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_union_territories_of_India "States and union territories of India") of [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat"). It is the administrative headquarters of the [Ahmedabad district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad_district "Ahmedabad district") and the seat of the [Gujarat High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_High_Court "Gujarat High Court"). Ahmedabad's population of 5,570,585 (per the 2011 population census) makes it the [sixth-most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_India_by_population "List of cities in India by population") in India,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-15) and the encompassing [urban area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_area "Urban area") population estimated at 8,854,444 (as of 2024) is the [seventh-most populous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_million-plus_urban_agglomerations_in_India "List of million-plus urban agglomerations in India") in India.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-16) Ahmedabad is located near the banks of the [Sabarmati River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabarmati_River "Sabarmati River"),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-citypop_India_aggs-17)25 km (16 mi)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-citypop_world_aggs-18) from the capital of [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat"), [Gandhinagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandhinagar "Gandhinagar"), also known as its twin city.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-19)

Ahmedabad has emerged as an important economic, industrial and cultural hub in India. It is the second-largest producer of [cotton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotton "Cotton") in India, due to which it was known as the "[Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester "Manchester") of India" along with [Kanpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanpur "Kanpur"). The [Ahmedabad Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad_Stock_Exchange "Ahmedabad Stock Exchange") (before it was shut down in 2018) was the country's second-oldest. [Cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") is a popular sport in Ahmedabad; the [Narendra Modi Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi_Stadium "Narendra Modi Stadium") at [Motera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motera "Motera") can accommodate 132,000 spectators, making it the [largest stadium in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stadiums_by_capacity "List of stadiums by capacity"). The [Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Sports Enclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardar_Vallabhbhai_Patel_Sports_Enclave "Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Sports Enclave") located near the stadium will be one of the biggest in the country once complete. Ahmedabad will host the [2030 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2030_Commonwealth_Games "2030 Commonwealth Games").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-20)

The effects of the [liberalisation of the Indian economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_liberalisation_in_India "Economic liberalisation in India") have energised the city's economy towards [tertiary sector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tertiary_sector "Tertiary sector") activities such as commerce, communication and construction.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-jnnurm-21) Ahmedabad's increasing population has increased demand in the construction and housing industries, resulting in the development of skyscrapers.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-Ahmadabad_joins_ITES_hot_spots-22)

In 2010, Ahmedabad was ranked third in _[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")_'s list of fastest growing cities of the decade.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-23) In 2012, _[The Times of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times\_of\_India "The Times of India")_ chose Ahmedabad as India's best city to live in.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-best_city_to_in_which_to_live_in_India-24) The gross domestic product of Ahmedabad metro was estimated at $136.1 billion in 2023.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-auto-14)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-25) In 2020, Ahmedabad was ranked as the third-best city in India to live in by the Ease of Living Index.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-26) In July 2022, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ magazine included Ahmedabad in its list of the world's 50 greatest places of 2022.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-27)

Ahmedabad has been selected as one of the hundred Indian cities to be developed as a [smart city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_city "Smart city") under the [Government of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India")'s flagship [Smart Cities Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_Cities_Mission "Smart Cities Mission").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-28) In July 2017, the [historic city of Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historic_City_of_Ahmadabad "Historic City of Ahmadabad"), or Old Ahmedabad, was declared a [UNESCO World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-29)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ahmedabad&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Main article: [History of Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Ahmedabad "History of Ahmedabad")

### Toponymy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ahmedabad&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Toponymy")]

Based on relics found in several neighbourhoods of the old city and on writings of the Persian historian [al-Biruni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Biruni "Al-Biruni"), it is surmised that an early [Bhil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhil "Bhil") tribal group settlement was known as [Ashaval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashaval "Ashaval").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMichellShah198817-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBobbio2015164-31)

According to [Merutunga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merutunga "Merutunga"), [Karna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karna_I "Karna I"), the [Chaulukya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaulukya_dynasty "Chaulukya dynasty") (Solanki) ruler of [Anhilwada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anhilwada "Anhilwada") (modern [Patan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patan,_Gujarat "Patan, Gujarat")), successfully launched a military campaign against [Ashaval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashaval "Ashaval") and founded a city nearby called Karnavati.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMichellShah198817-30) The location of Karnavati is not definitively known.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBobbio2015164-31) References from the 14th and 15th centuries mention Ashaval but do not mention Karnavati.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBobbio2015164-31)

[Ahmad Shah I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Shah_I "Ahmad Shah I") of the [Gujarat Sultanate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Sultanate "Gujarat Sultanate") transferred its capital from Anhilvada to Ashaval in 1411 CE; as was customary, the city was subsequently renamed Ahmedabad after the Sultan.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMichellShah198818-32)

### Early history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ahmedabad&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early history")]

The area around Ahmedabad has been inhabited since the 11th century, when it was known as _[Ashaval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashaval "Ashaval")_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-33) At that time, [Karna I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karna_I "Karna I"), the [Chaulukya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaulukya_dynasty "Chaulukya dynasty") (Solanki) ruler of Anhilwara (modern [Patan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patan,_Gujarat "Patan, Gujarat")), waged a successful war against the [Bhil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhil "Bhil") king of Ashaval,[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-34) and established a city called _Karnavati_ on the banks of the Sabarmati.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-Madan-35) Solanki rule lasted until the 13th century, when Gujarat came under the control of the [Vaghela dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaghela_dynasty "Vaghela dynasty") of [Dholka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dholka "Dholka"). Gujarat subsequently came under the control of the [Delhi Sultanate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_Sultanate "Delhi Sultanate") in the 14th century. However, by the early 15th century, the local Muslim governor Zafar Khan Muzaffar established his independence from the Delhi Sultanate and crowned himself [Sultan of Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Sultanate "Gujarat Sultanate") as [Muzaffar Shah I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muzaffar_Shah_I "Muzaffar Shah I"), thereby founding the [Muzaffarid dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muzaffarids_(Gujarat) "Muzaffarids (Gujarat)").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-:2-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-sen2-38) In 1411, the area came under the control of his grandson, Sultan [Ahmed Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Shah_I "Ahmad Shah I"), who selected the forested area along the banks of the Sabarmati river for his new capital. He laid the foundation of a new walled city near Karnavati and named it Ahmedabad after himself.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-baba-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-40) According to other versions, he named the city after four Muslim saints in the area who all had the name Ahmed.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-AMC_History-41) Ahmed Shah I laid the foundation of the city on 26 February 1411[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-Pandya_2010-42) (at 1.20 pm, Thursday, the second day of [Dhu'l-Qa'da](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhu'l-Qa'da "Dhu'l-Qa'da"), [Hijri era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hijri_era "Hijri era") 813[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-43)) at [Manek Burj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manek_Burj "Manek Burj"). Manek Burj is named after the legendary 15th-century Hindu saint, [Maneknath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maneknath "Maneknath"), who intervened to help [Ahmad Shah I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Shah_I "Ahmad Shah I") build [Bhadra Fort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhadra_Fort "Bhadra Fort") in 1411.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-baba-39)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-igg-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-mnk-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-tam-46) Ahmed Shah I chose it as the new capital on 4 March 1411.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-47) Chandan and Rajesh Nath, 13th generation descendants of Saint Maneknath, perform _[puja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puja\_(Hinduism) "Puja (Hinduism)")_ and hoist the flag on Manek Burj on Ahmedabad's foundation day and for the [Vijayadashami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayadashami "Vijayadashami") festival every year.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-baba-39)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-mnk-45)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-India_2015-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-dnax2011-49)

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/City_Walls_of_Ahmedabad_page-0001.jpg/250px-City_Walls_of_Ahmedabad_page-0001.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:City_Walls_of_Ahmedabad_page-0001.jpg)

City walls of Ahmedabad, 1866

In 1487, [Mahmud Begada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahmud_Begada "Mahmud Begada"), the great-great-grandson of Ahmed Shah, fortified the city with an outer wall 10 km (6.2 mi) in circumference and consisting of [twelve gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gates_of_Ahmedabad "Gates of Ahmedabad"), 189 bastions, and over 6,000 battlements.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-50) In 1535 [Humayun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humayun "Humayun") briefly occupied Ahmedabad after capturing [Champaner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champaner "Champaner") when the ruler of Gujarat, [Bahadur Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahadur_Shah_of_Gujarat "Bahadur Shah of Gujarat"), fled to [Diu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diu,_India "Diu, India").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-51) Ahmedabad was then reoccupied by the Muzaffarid dynasty until 1573 when Gujarat was conquered by the [Mughal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal_Empire "Mughal Empire") emperor [Akbar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar "Akbar"). During the Mughal reign, Ahmedabad became one of the Empire's thriving centres of trade, mainly in textiles, which were exported as far as Europe. The Mughal ruler [Shah Jahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Jahan "Shah Jahan") spent the prime of his life in the city, sponsoring the construction of the [Moti Shahi Mahal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardar_Vallabhbhai_Patel_National_Memorial "Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Memorial") in [Shahibaug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahibaug "Shahibaug"). The [Deccan famine of 1630–1632](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deccan_famine_of_1630%E2%80%931632 "Deccan famine of 1630–1632") affected the city, as did famines in 1650 and 1686.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-52) Ahmedabad remained the provincial headquarters of the Mughals until 1758, when they surrendered the city to the [Maratha Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-53)

### Modern history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ahmedabad&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Modern history")]

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/1901_Ahmedabadi_Market.jpg/250px-1901_Ahmedabadi_Market.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1901_Ahmedabadi_Market.jpg)

A market scene in Ahmedabad, 1901

During the period of Maratha governance, the city became the centre of a conflict between the [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa") of [Poona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pune "Pune") and the [Gaekwad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaekwad_dynasty "Gaekwad dynasty") of [Baroda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vadodara "Vadodara").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-GNHistory-54) In 1780, during the [First Anglo-Maratha War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Anglo-Maratha_War "First Anglo-Maratha War"), a British force under [James Hartley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Hartley_(East_India_Company_officer) "James Hartley (East India Company officer)") stormed and captured Ahmedabad, but it was handed back to the Marathas at the end of the war. The [East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_India_Company "East India Company") took over the city in 1818 during the [Third Anglo-Maratha War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Anglo-Maratha_War "Third Anglo-Maratha War").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-AMC_History-41) A military cantonment was established in 1824, and a municipal government in 1858.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-AMC_History-41) Incorporated into the [Bombay Presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay_Presidency "Bombay Presidency") during [British rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj"), Ahmedabad became one of the most important cities in the Gujarat region. In 1864, a railway link between Ahmedabad and [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai") (then Bombay) was established by the [Bombay, Baroda and Central India Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay,_Baroda_and_Central_India_Railway "Bombay, Baroda and Central India Railway") (BB&CI), enabling traffic and trade between [northern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_India "North India") and [southern India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_India "South India") via the city.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-AMC_History-41) Over time, the city established itself as the home of a developing textile industry, which earned it the nickname "Manchester of India".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-BordenFraser2014-55)

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/Ahmedabad_%28Baedeker%2C_1914%29.jpg/250px-Ahmedabad_%28Baedeker%2C_1914%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ahmedabad_(Baedeker,_1914).jpg)

Ahmedabad and its environs, ca 1914

The [Indian independence movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_independence_movement "Indian independence movement") developed roots in the city when [Mahatma Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahatma_Gandhi "Mahatma Gandhi") established two [ashrams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashram "Ashram")– the [Kochrab Ashram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kochrab_Ashram "Kochrab Ashram") near [Paldi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paldi_(Ahmedabad) "Paldi (Ahmedabad)") in 1915 and the Satyagraha Ashram (now [Sabarmati Ashram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabarmati_Ashram "Sabarmati Ashram")) on the banks of the Sabarmati in 1917– which would become centres of nationalist activities.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-AMC_History-41)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-manchester-56) During the [mass protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-cooperation_movement_(1919%E2%80%931922) "Non-cooperation movement (1919–1922)") against the [Rowlatt Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anarchical_and_Revolutionary_Crimes_Act,_1919 "Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, 1919") in 1919, textile workers burned down 51 government buildings across the city in protest against a British attempt to extend wartime regulations after the [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"). In the 1920s, textile workers and teachers went on strike, demanding civil rights and better pay and working conditions. In 1930, Gandhi initiated the [Salt March](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_March "Salt March") from Ahmedabad by embarking from his ashram on the Dandi March. The city's administration and economic institutions were rendered inoperative in the early 1930s by the large numbers of people who took to the streets in peaceful protests, and again in 1942 during the [Quit India Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quit_India_Movement "Quit India Movement").

#### Post-independence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ahmedabad&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Post-independence")]

Following independence and the [partition of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_India "Partition of India") in 1947, the city was scarred by the intense communal violence that broke out between [Hindus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindus "Hindus") and [Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslims "Muslims") in 1947. Ahmedabad was the focus of settlement by Hindu migrants from Pakistan,[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-GillyGilinskiy2009-57) who expanded the city's population and transformed its demographics and economy.

By 1960, Ahmedabad had become a metropolis with a population of over one million people, with classical and colonial European-style buildings lining the city's thoroughfares.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-Ghurye1962-58) It was chosen as the capital of Gujarat after the partition of the [Bombay State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay_State "Bombay State") on 1 May 1960.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-Y%C4%81j%C3%B1ikaSheth2005-59) During this period, a large number of educational and research institutions were founded in the city, making it a centre for [higher education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education_in_India "Education in India"), science, and technology.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-Political_Science-60) Ahmedabad's economic base became more diverse with the establishment of heavy and chemical industry during the same period.

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/Gandhi_Ashram.jpg/250px-Gandhi_Ashram.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gandhi_Ashram.jpg)

[Sabarmati Ashram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabarmati_Ashram "Sabarmati Ashram"), established by [Mahatma Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahatma_Gandhi "Mahatma Gandhi")

In the late 1970s, the capital shifted to the newly built city of [Gandhinagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandhinagar "Gandhinagar"). This marked the start of a long period of decline in Ahmedabad, marked by a lack of development. The 1974 _[Navnirman Andolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navnirman\_Andolan "Navnirman Andolan")_ agitation, a protest against a 20% hike in the hostel food fees at the [Lalbhai Dalpatbhai College of Engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lalbhai_Dalpatbhai_College_of_Engineering "Lalbhai Dalpatbhai College of Engineering") in Ahmedabad, snowballed into a movement to remove [Chimanbhai Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chimanbhai_Patel "Chimanbhai Patel"), then [Chief Minister of Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Minister_of_Gujarat "Chief Minister of Gujarat").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-61) In the 1980s, a [reservation policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reservation_in_India "Reservation in India") was introduced in the country, which led to anti-reservation protests in 1981 and 1985. The protests witnessed violent clashes between people belonging to various [castes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caste_system_in_India "Caste system in India").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-62) The city was considerably impacted by the [2001 Gujarat earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake "2001 Gujarat earthquake"); up to 50 multi-storey buildings collapsed, killing 752 people and causing significant damage.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-63) The following year, three days of violence between Hindus and Muslims in the western Indian state of Gujarat, known as the [2002 Gujarat violence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Gujarat_violence "2002 Gujarat violence"), spread to Ahmedabad; in eastern [Chamanpura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chamanpura "Chamanpura"), 69 people were killed in the [Gulbarg Society massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulbarg_Society_massacre "Gulbarg Society massacre") on 28 February 2002.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-Gulbarg-64) Refugee camps were set up around the city, housing 50,000 Muslims, as well as some small Hindu camps.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-65)

The [2008 Ahmedabad bombings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Ahmedabad_bombings "2008 Ahmedabad bombings"), a series of seventeen bomb blasts, killed and injured many people.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-66) The terrorist group [Harkat-ul-Jihad al-Islami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harkat-ul-Jihad_al-Islami "Harkat-ul-Jihad al-Islami") claimed responsibility for the attacks.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-67) In 2020, the city hosted the _[Namaste Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namaste\_Trump "Namaste Trump")_ event at the newly built [Narendra Modi Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi_Stadium "Narendra Modi Stadium"), the [world's largest cricket stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cricket_grounds_by_capacity "List of cricket grounds by capacity") as well as the [largest overall stadium in the world by capacity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stadiums_by_capacity "List of stadiums by capacity").

## Demographics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ahmedabad&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Demographics")]

City population increased by 23.43% from 4,519,000 as of the [2001 census of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_census_of_India "2001 census of India")[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ahmedabad&action=edit) to 5,577,940 (2,938,985 males and 2,638,955 females resulting in a sex ratio of 898 females per 1,000 males) as of the [2011 census of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_census_of_India "2011 census of India")[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ahmedabad&action=edit) making Ahmedabad the [fifth most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_India_by_population "List of cities in India by population") in India.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-:3-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-:4-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-70) The [Urban area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_area "Urban area") centred upon Ahmedabad had a population of 6,352,254 and was the [seventh most populous urban agglomeration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_million-plus_urban_agglomerations_in_India "List of million-plus urban agglomerations in India") in India as of the [2011 census of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_census_of_India "2011 census of India")[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ahmedabad&action=edit).[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-:4-69)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-71) The population of children aged 0 to 6 was 621,034 (336,063 males and 284,971 females resulting in a child sex ratio of 848 females per 1,000 males) as of the [2011 census of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_census_of_India "2011 census of India")[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ahmedabad&action=edit).[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-:3-68) The city had an average [literacy rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literacy_in_India "Literacy in India") of 88.29%, a male literacy rate of 92.30%, and a female literacy rate of 83.85%.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-:3-68)

The estimated population of Ahmedabad city is 7,692,000, while that of the urban agglomeration area is 8,772,000 as of 2023.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-:3-68) The [2021 census of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2027_census_of_India "2027 census of India") has been delayed to 2024-25, and the deadline to freeze administrative boundaries has been extended to 1 January 2024.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad#cite_note-72) As of now, it has further been extended to 2027.

### Poverty

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ahmedabad&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Poverty")]

In the mid-1970s and early 1980s, the textile mills that were responsible for much of Ahmedabad's wealth faced competition from automation and domestic speciality looms. Several mills closed down, leaving between 40,000 and 50,000 people without a source of income, and many moved into informal settlements in the city centre. The [Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad_Municipal_Corporation "Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation") (AMC), the governing and administrative body of the city, simultaneously lost much of its tax base and saw an increased demand for services.

**[Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram") Parliamentary (Lok Sabha) Constituency** is one of the 20 parliamentary constituencies in Kerala, India. It is located in [Thiruvananthapuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district "Thiruvananthapuram district") and encompasses the major part of [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram") city, the capital of [Kerala State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala").

The incumbent MP of this constituency, [Shashi Tharoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor "Shashi Tharoor") of the [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress"), has been elected on 4 consecutive occasions: 2009, 2014, 2019 and 2024. He is the longest serving Member of Parliament to have represented the constituency.

## Demographics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Demographics")]

This constituency is dominated By [Nair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nair "Nair") and [Nadar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-2) As per the electoral roll for the 2024 polls, the total electorate is of 14,03,281 people including 7,27,469 women, 6,75,771 men and 41 transgender people.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-3) Out of total electorate, 26% is rural and 74% is urban. The Scheduled castes (SC) and Scheduled tribes (ST) is 9.82% and 0.45%, respectively of total electorate.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-4) The constituency also has highest proportion of [Nadars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)") and [Converted Christians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conversion_to_Christianity "Conversion to Christianity") in Kerala.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-5)[Nairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nair "Nair") dominates the urban segments of [Kazhakootam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazhakootam_Assembly_constituency "Kazhakootam Assembly constituency"),[Nemom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemom_Assembly_constituency "Nemom Assembly constituency"),[Vattiyoorkavu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vattiyoorkavu_Assembly_constituency "Vattiyoorkavu Assembly constituency") and [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Assembly_constituency "Thiruvananthapuram Assembly constituency") While the [Nadars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)") are Concentrated on [Neyyattinkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyattinkara_Assembly_constituency "Neyyattinkara Assembly constituency"),[Parassala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parassala_Assembly_constituency "Parassala Assembly constituency"),[Kovalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kovalam_Assembly_constituency "Kovalam Assembly constituency").

As per the voter list published by the Election commission for the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, there were 13,34,665 voters in the electorate and 1077 polling stations in this constituency.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-ceo.kerala.gov.in-6) The voter turnout for the 2019 Lok Sabha election was 73.45% where as it was 68.63% and 65.74% in the 2014 and 2009 elections respectively.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-7)

Thiruvananthapuram (Malayalam pronunciation: [t̪iɾuʋənən̪d̪ɐˈbuɾəm] ⓘ tirr-ROO-və-nun-Tə-poor-əm), also known as Trivandrum, is the capital city of the Indian state of Kerala.[9][10] As of 2011, the Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation had a population of 957,730 over an area of 214.86 km2,[11] making it the most populous city in Kerala.[12] The larger Thiruvananthapuram metropolitan area has over 1.7 million inhabitants within an area of 543 km2, making it the second-most populous metropolitan area in Kerala after Kochi.[13]. Thiruvananthapuram is one of the few cities in India that serves as a state capital and is also centre for heritage, maritime activities, information technology, research and development, space research, defence, automotive technology, and biosciences. It is also among the few cities in the world where both an international airport and an international seaport are located within the city in close proximity to the city centre.[14]

Located on the west coast of India near the extreme south of the mainland, Thiruvananthapuram is a port city located 10 nautical miles (19 km; 12 mi)[15] from a heavily trafficked east–west shipping channel. The city is home to India's first deep-water trans-shipment port, owned by the Vizhinjam International Seaport Ltd. Thiruvananthapuram under the Government of Kerala.[16] The city is characterised by its undulating terrain of low coastal hills.[17] Thiruvananthapuram is also known for its cultural heritage, being associated with the musical contributions of Swathi Thirunal Rama Varma and the artistic legacy of painter Raja Ravi Varma. Thiruvananthapuram has contributed to the development of Malayalam literature through individuals like Ulloor S. Parameswara Iyer, Kumaran Asan, C. V. Raman Pillai and Narayana Guru. The city is also known for Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, known as the richest temple in the world.[18] The other temples includes the Sreevaraham temple, the Shreekanteswaram temple and the Attukal Bhagavathy temple.

The present regions that constitute Thiruvananthapuram were ruled by the Ays who were related to feudatories of the Chera dynasty.[19] In the 12th century, it was conquered by the Kingdom of Venad.[19] In the 18th century, the king Marthanda Varma expanded the territory, founded the princely state of Travancore and made Thiruvananthapuram its capital.[20] Travancore became the most dominant state in Kerala by defeating the powerful Zamorin of Calicut in the battle of Purakkad in 1755.[21] Following India's independence in 1947, Thiruvananthapuram became the capital of Travancore–Cochin state and remained so until the new Indian state of Kerala was formed in 1956.[22][23]

Thiruvananthapuram is a notable academic and research hub and home to the University of Kerala, APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University, the regional headquarters of Indira Gandhi National Open University, and many other schools and colleges. Thiruvananthapuram is also home to research centres such as the National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology, the Indian Space Research Organisation's Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, the Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology, the National Centre for Earth Science Studies and a campus of the Indian Institutes of Science Education and Research.[24] Thiruvananthapuram is where India's space programme began, with the headquarters of Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre located there. The city is home to media institutions like Toonz Animation India and Tata Elxsi Ltd, and also to Chitranjali Film Studio, one of the first film studios in Malayalam Cinema, and Kinfra Film and Video Park at Kazhakoottam, which is India's first infotainment industrial park.[25]

In 2012, Thiruvananthapuram was named the best Kerala city to live in, by a field survey conducted by The Times of India.[26] In 2013, the city was ranked the fifteenth best city to live in in India, in a survey conducted by India Today.[27] Thiruvananthapuram was ranked the best Indian city for two consecutive years, 2015 and 2016, according to the Annual Survey of India's City-Systems (ASICS) conducted by the Janaagraha Centre for Citizenship and Democracy.[28] The city was also selected as the best governed city in India in a survey conducted by Janaagraha Centre for citizenship and democracy in 2017.[29]

Etymologyedit

The city takes its name from the Malayalam word thiru-anantha-puram (തിരുവനന്തപുരം [t̪iɾuʋɐnɐn̪d̪ɐpuɾɐm] ⓘ), meaning "The City of Lord Anantha (means infinite, endless, or eternal)",[30] referring to the deity of the Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple located in the city. Thiruvananthapuram is also known in literature, and popular reference as Ananthapuri, derived from the Sanskrit word Syanandurapuram, meaning "The City of Bliss" in Carnatic kirtanas composed by Swathi Thirunal, erstwhile Maharaja of Travancore.[31] The city was officially referred to as Trivandrum until 1991 (Trivandrum being the anglicised name of the town), when the government decided to reinstate the city's original name Thiruvananthapuram. Many Malayalees still refer to the city as Trivandrum, however.[32] The city was also called as Anandapatnam or Anandapatam in Tamil and Telugu, meaning "The City of Ananda" which has the same meaning as the original name. [citation needed]
